title.zh: 卷十三 列傳第七 范雲 沈約
title.raw: 卷十三 列傳第七 范雲 沈約 Volume 13: Fan Yun; Shen Yue

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十三 列傳第七

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7

sentences.zh: 范雲 沈約

translations.literal: Fan Yun; Shen Yue
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun; Shen Yue

sentences.zh: 范雲字彥龍，南鄉舞陰人，晉平北將軍汪六世孫也。

translations.literal: Fan Yun, styled Yanlong, was a native of Wuyin in Nanxiang, sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Pacifier of the North General Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun, styled Yanlong, came from Wuyin in Nanxiang—a sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Pacifier of the North, Wang.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，遇宋豫州刺史殷琰於塗，琰異之，要就席，雲風姿應對，傍若無人。

translations.literal: At eight he met Song's Inspector of Yuzhou Yin Yan on the road; Yan was struck by him and had him sit; Yun's bearing and replies were as if no one else were there.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he met Yin Yan, Song's Yuzhou inspector, on the road; Yan was amazed and asked him to sit; Yun answered with easy grace, as though the crowd were empty.

sentences.zh: 琰令賦詩，操筆便就，坐者歎焉。

translations.literal: Yan had him compose a poem; he took up the brush and finished at once—the company marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked him to write a poem; he took brush and finished on the spot, and all who sat there sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 嘗就親人袁照學，晝夜不怠。

translations.literal: He once studied with his kinsman Yuan Zhao and did not slacken day or night.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his kinsman Yuan Zhao, laboring day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 照撫其背曰：「卿精神秀朗而勤於學，卿相才也。

translations.literal: Zhao stroked his back and said, "Your spirit is bright and clear, and you study without cease—you have the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stroked his back and said, "Your spirit shines, and you study without rest—you are minister material.

sentences.zh: 」少機警，有識具，善屬文，便尺牘，下筆輒成，未嘗定藁，時人每疑其宿構。

translations.literal: " In youth he was quick-witted and discerning, skilled at literary composition and at letters; whatever he wrote came out at once, never with a fixed draft—men often suspected he had prepared the piece overnight.
translations.idiomatic: " As a boy he was sharp and far-seeing, good at prose and at correspondence; his pen never paused for a draft, and contemporaries often thought he must have written the piece the night before.

sentences.zh: 父抗，爲郢府參軍，雲隨父在府，時吳興沈約、新野庾杲之與抗同府，見而友之。

translations.literal: His father Kang was a staff officer in the Ying headquarters; Yun followed his father to the post, when Wu-xing's Shen Yue and Xinye's Yu Gao, who served with Kang in the same office, saw him and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang served on the Ying staff; Yun went with him, and Shen Yue of Wu-xing and Yu Gao of Xinye, who shared Kang's office, met him and became his friends.

sentences.zh: 起家郢州西曹書佐，轉法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He first entered office as Western Bureau secretary in Yingzhou, then was transferred to acting legal-affairs staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Yingzhou western bureau secretary, then became acting legal-affairs staff officer.

sentences.zh: 俄而沈攸之舉兵圍郢城，抗時爲府長流，入城固守，留家屬居外。

translations.literal: Before long Shen Youzhi raised troops and besieged Ying city; Kang was then the headquarters chief clerk and entered the city to hold it fast, leaving his household outside.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shen Youzhi rebelled and besieged Ying; Kang, as headquarters chief clerk, went into the city to defend it and left his family outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 雲爲軍人所得，攸之召與語，聲色甚厲，雲容貌不變，徐自陳說。

translations.literal: Yun was taken by the besiegers; Youzhi summoned him to speak, his voice and face fierce, yet Yun's countenance did not change as he slowly made his case.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was seized by Youzhi's soldiers; Youzhi called him in, harsh in voice and face, but Yun's expression never shifted as he pleaded his case at leisure.

sentences.zh: 攸之乃笑曰：「卿定可兒，且出就舍。

translations.literal: Youzhi then laughed and said, "You are surely a promising boy. For now, go to the barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi laughed and said, "You are surely a boy who will amount to something. Go back to quarters for now.

sentences.zh: 」明旦，又召令送書入城。

translations.literal: " The next morning he summoned him again and ordered him to carry a letter into the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Next day he called him again and sent him into the city with a message.

sentences.zh: 城內或欲誅之，雲曰：「老母弱弟，懸命沈氏，若違其命，禍必及親，今日就戮，甘心如薺。

translations.literal: Some inside the city wished to execute him; Yun said, "My aged mother and young brother hang on Shen's mercy; if I disobey his order, disaster will reach my kin—today I go to the blade, and my heart is as mustard greens."
translations.idiomatic: Men in the city wanted to kill him; Yun said, "Mother and brother depend on the Shen clan; defy him and kin will suffer—let me die today, and I am content."

sentences.zh: 」長史柳世隆素與雲善，乃免之。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Liu Shilong had long been friendly with Yun and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Liu Shilong, who had always been close to Yun, had him spared.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，竟陵王子良爲會稽太守，雲始隨王，王未之知也。

translations.literal: Early in Qi's Jianyuan era the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, was prefect of Kuaiji; Yun first followed the prince, who did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qi's Jianyuan reign the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, held Kuaiji; Yun joined his suite before the prince had noticed him.

sentences.zh: 會游秦望，使人視刻石文，時莫能識，雲獨誦之，王悅，自是寵冠府朝。

translations.literal: Once, touring Mount Qinwang, the prince sent men to read an inscription on stone; none could make it out, but Yun alone recited it; the prince was pleased, and from then on Yun stood first in favor throughout the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Mount Qinwang the prince had the carved stone read; no one could decipher it until Yun recited it whole; the prince delighted in him, and thereafter Yun led the court of the prince's house.

sentences.zh: 王爲丹陽尹，召爲主簿，深相親任。

translations.literal: When the prince became metropolitan governor, Yun was summoned as chief clerk and drawn into deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became metropolitan governor he made Yun chief clerk and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時進見齊高帝，值有獻白烏者，帝問此爲何瑞？

translations.literal: Once, on an audience with Qi Emperor Gao, someone presented a white crow; the emperor asked what omen this was.
translations.idiomatic: On one audience with Qi Emperor Gao a white crow was offered; the emperor asked what sign it portended.

sentences.zh: 雲位卑，最後答曰：「臣聞王者敬宗廟，則白烏至。

translations.literal: Yun, lowest in rank, answered last: "I have heard that when a king honors his ancestral temples, the white crow comes.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, last in rank because he stood low, answered: "I have heard that when a true king reveres his ancestral shrines, the white crow appears.

sentences.zh: 」時謁廟始畢。

translations.literal: " The temple rites had just been completed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court had only just finished paying temple homage.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You speak rightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words are right.

sentences.zh: 感應之理，一至此乎！

translations.literal: Can the logic of resonance reach so far!
translations.idiomatic: Can responsive principle run so deep!

sentences.zh: 」轉補征北南郡王刑獄參軍事，領主簿如故，遷尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to supplemental staff officer for criminal matters under the Prince of Northern Campaign's southern commandery, retaining his chief-clerk post; he was promoted to palace bureau director within the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He became supplemental criminal-affairs officer to the southern commandery prince of the northern campaign, still chief clerk, then rose to secretariat palace bureau director.

sentences.zh: 子良爲司徒，又補記室參軍事，尋授通直散騎侍郎、領本州大中正。

translations.literal: When Zi Liang became Minister of Education, Yun was again made record-keeper staff officer, then given regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and charge as grand coordinator of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi Liang became minister of education Yun was record-keeper on his staff, then regular scattered-cavalry attendant and head of the provincial grand coordinator's office.

sentences.zh: 出爲零陵內史，在任潔己，省煩苛，去游費，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He went out as interior magistrate of Lingling; in office he kept himself clean, cut redundant rules, and abolished pleasure spending—the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Lingling interior magistrate, lived plainly, stripped away petty regulations and travel costs, and the district rested easy under him.

sentences.zh: 明帝召還都，及至，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming recalled him to the capital; when he arrived he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming called him back to court; on arrival he was made regular scattered-cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 復出爲始興內史。

translations.literal: He went out again as interior magistrate of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as Shixing interior magistrate.

sentences.zh: 郡多豪猾大姓，二千石有不善者，謀共殺害，不則逐去之。

translations.literal: The commandery held many powerful clans; when a magistrate of two thousand bushels displeased them, they plotted to kill him—or, failing that, to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture teemed with great houses; when a two-thousand-bushel magistrate failed them, they plotted murder, or else expulsion.

sentences.zh: 邊帶蠻俚，尤多盜賊，前內史皆以兵刃自衛。

translations.literal: On the frontier barbarians and Liao peoples abounded, and bandits were especially numerous; earlier magistrates had all gone armed.
translations.idiomatic: The border swarmed with tribal peoples and thieves; every prior magistrate had marched with weapons.

sentences.zh: 雲入境，撫以恩德，罷亭候，商賈露宿，郡中稱爲神明。

translations.literal: When Yun entered his post he ruled by kindness and trust, abolished watch-posts, and merchants slept in the open—the commandery called him a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yun entered and ruled with grace, lifted the guard posts, and traders camped in the open road; the district hailed him as divine.

sentences.zh: 仍遷假節、建武將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted acting commissioner, General Who Establishes Martial Glory, Colonel Pacifying the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held acting credentials, was General Who Establishes Martial Glory, colonel pacifying the Yue, and Guangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 初，雲與尚書僕射江祏善，祏姨弟徐藝爲曲江令，深以託雲。

translations.literal: Earlier Yun had been close to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang You; You's cousin on his mother's side, Xu Yi, was magistrate of Qujiang, and Jiang deeply entrusted him to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had been friendly with vice director Jiang You; You's maternal cousin Xu Yi was Qujiang magistrate, and Jiang pressed Yun to watch over him.

sentences.zh: 有譚儼者，縣之豪族，藝鞭之，儼以爲恥，詣京訴雲，雲坐徵還下獄，會赦免。

translations.literal: A certain Tan Yan, a powerful man of the county, was flogged by Yi; Yan took it as shame and went to the capital to accuse Yun; Yun was recalled and imprisoned, then freed when an amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yan, a county magnate, was beaten by Yi; shamed, he went to the capital to denounce Yun, who was recalled, jailed, and released by general pardon.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，起爲國子博士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year two he was made national university erudite.

sentences.zh: 初，雲與高祖遇於齊竟陵王子良邸，又嘗接里閈，高祖深器之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yun had met Gaozu at the residence of Qi's Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, and had also been a neighbor; Gaozu prized him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Yun had met Gaozu at Prince of Jingling Zi Liang's mansion and had lived near him; Gaozu held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及義兵至京邑，雲時在城內。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital, Yun was inside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army came to the capital Yun was still within the city.

sentences.zh: 東昏旣誅，侍中張稷使雲銜命出城，高祖因留之，便參帷幄，仍拜黃門侍郎，與沈約同心翊贊。

translations.literal: After Dong Hun was killed, Attendant Within Zhang Ji had Yun carry orders out of the city; Gaozu kept him and made him counsel in the command tent, then Yellow Gate Attendant—he and Shen Yue worked as one heart to support the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun fell; Zhang Ji sent Yun out of the city with orders; Gaozu detained him for his war council, made him yellow gate attendant, and he and Shen Yue joined in loyal support.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大司馬諮議參軍、領錄事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to staff officer of the Grand Marshal's advisory section with charge of registry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was grand marshal advisory staff officer in charge of registry.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was made attendant within.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang court was set up he became attendant within.

sentences.zh: 時高祖納齊東昏余妃，頗妨政事，雲嘗以爲言，未之納也。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu took Dong Hun's former consort, which somewhat hindered state affairs; Yun spoke of it more than once, but his words were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had taken Dong Hun's former consort, and it tangled government; Yun spoke against it repeatedly, without success.

sentences.zh: 後與王茂同入臥內，雲又諫曰：「昔漢祖居山東，貪財好色，及入關定秦，財帛無所取，婦女無所幸，范增以爲其志大故也。

translations.literal: Later, entering the sleeping quarters with Wang Mao, Yun remonstrated again: "Of old, when Han's founding ancestor dwelt east of the mountains, he was greedy for goods and fond of women; when he entered the passes and pacified Qin, he seized no wealth and kept no woman—Fan Zeng took that as proof his ambition was great.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went into the inner quarters with Wang Mao and urged again: "Han's founding ancestor, east of the mountains, loved gold and women; once he entered the passes and settled Qin he touched no treasure and kept no woman—Fan Zeng read that as greatness of purpose.

sentences.zh: 今明公始定天下，海內想望風聲，奈何襲昏亂之蹤，以女德爲累。

translations.literal: Now, Illustrious Lord, you have only just settled the realm; all within the seas look to your reputation—how can you tread the path of a dissolute age and let a woman's charm weigh you down?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you have only just won the realm; the world watches your bearing—why repeat the tracks of a ruined court and let a woman's grace become your burden?"

sentences.zh: 」王茂因起拜曰：「范雲言是，公必以天下爲念，無宜留惜。

translations.literal: Wang Mao rose and bowed: "Fan Yun speaks rightly; you must keep the realm in mind and should not hold back for sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao stood and bowed: "Fan Yun is right; the lord must think of the realm and must not cling to private feeling."

sentences.zh: 」高祖默然。

translations.literal: Gaozu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said nothing.

sentences.zh: 雲便疏令以余氏賚茂，高祖賢其意而許之。

translations.literal: Yun at once memorialized to have the former consort given to Mao as a reward; Gaozu admired his intent and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun promptly memorialized to grant the former consort to Mao; Gaozu praised his purpose and assented.

sentences.zh: 明日，賜雲、茂錢各百萬。

translations.literal: The next day he bestowed on Yun and Mao a hundred thousand cash each.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he gave Yun and Mao each a hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，高祖受禪，柴燎於南郊，雲以侍中參乘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, Gaozu received the abdication; at the southern suburb he offered the fire sacrifice, with Yun as attendant within riding in the secondary carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one Gaozu took the throne; at the southern suburb fire rite Yun rode as attendant within in the secondary carriage.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，高祖升輦，謂雲曰：「朕之今日，所謂懍乎若朽索之馭六馬。

translations.literal: When the rites ended Gaozu ascended the imperial carriage and said to Yun, "For me today is what they call driving six horses with rotten rope."
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended Gaozu mounted the imperial carriage and told Yun, "Today I am like a man driving six horses on rotted reins."

sentences.zh: 」雲對曰：「亦願陛下日慎一日。

translations.literal: Yun replied, "I also hope Your Majesty will be more cautious day by day."
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered, "I only wish Your Majesty would grow more careful with each passing day."

sentences.zh: 」高祖善之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved his words.

sentences.zh: 是日，遷散騎常侍、吏部尚書；

translations.literal: That day he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and Minister of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: That day he became regular scattered-cavalry attendant and minister of personnel;

sentences.zh: 以佐命功封霄城縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: for his merit in founding the state he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: for founding merit he was made marquis of Xiaocheng with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 雲以舊恩見拔，超居佐命，盡誠翊亮，知無不爲。

translations.literal: Yun, raised for old friendship beyond his station in founding the state, gave his utmost in loyal service and did whatever he could.
translations.idiomatic: Lifted by old favor above his peers in the founding enterprise, Yun served with full loyalty and never held back.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦推心任之，所奏多允。

translations.literal: Gaozu also gave him his full trust; what he memorialized was mostly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu in turn trusted him completely; most of what he submitted was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，高祖謂臨川王宏、鄱陽王恢曰：「我與范尚書少親善，申四海之敬；

translations.literal: Once at a banquet Gaozu said to the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, and the Prince of Poyang, Hui: "In youth Fan, our Minister of Personnel, and I were close; we extended the courtesies of the four seas;
translations.idiomatic: At one feast Gaozu told Princes Hong of Linchuan and Hui of Poyang: "Minister Fan and I were intimate in youth—we honored one another as the realm demands;

sentences.zh: 今爲天下主，此禮旣革，汝宜代我呼范爲兄。

translations.literal: now that I am master of the realm this ceremony is changed—you should call Fan elder brother in my place."
translations.idiomatic: now I am sovereign and that rite is gone—you should call Fan elder brother for me."

sentences.zh: 」二王下席拜，與雲同車還尚書下省，時人榮之。

translations.literal: The two princes left their seats to bow; they returned with Yun in the same carriage to the Ministry of Personnel offices below court—men of the time counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Both princes rose, bowed, and rode back with Yun to the personnel ministry—contemporaries called it honor.

sentences.zh: 其年，東宮建，雲以本官領太子中庶子，尋遷尚書右僕射，猶領吏部。

translations.literal: That year the Eastern Palace was established; Yun retained his office and also became crown prince senior mentor; soon he was Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, still holding Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That year the heir apparent was installed; Yun kept his post and became crown prince senior mentor, then vice director of the masters of writing while still heading personnel.

sentences.zh: 頃之，坐違詔用人，免吏部，猶爲僕射。

translations.literal: Before long, for violating an edict in making appointments, he was removed from Personnel but remained vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for appointing men against imperial order, he lost personnel but kept the vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 雲性篤睦，事寡嫂盡禮，家事必先諮而後行。

translations.literal: Yun was warm by nature and treated his widowed sister-in-law with full ritual; household matters he always consulted her on before acting.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was dutiful and affectionate; he observed every courtesy toward his widowed sister-in-law and never acted at home until he had asked her.

sentences.zh: 好節尚奇，專趣人之急。

translations.literal: He loved restraint and the unusual and devoted himself to others' urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished integrity and the extraordinary and threw himself into others' crises.

sentences.zh: 少時與領軍長史王畡善，畡亡於官舍，貧無居宅，雲乃迎喪還家。

translations.literal: In youth he had been close to the leading army chief clerk Wang Kai; when Kai died in the official residence, poor and without a dwelling, Yun brought the coffin home himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was close to leading-army chief clerk Wang Kai; Kai died in his government quarters, destitute, without a house, and Yun brought the bier home.

sentences.zh: 躬營含殯。

translations.literal: He personally arranged the encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the burial rites himself.

sentences.zh: 事竟陵王子良恩禮甚隆，雲每獻損益，未嘗阿意。

translations.literal: Toward the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, his courtesy was very deep; whenever Yun offered advice on gain and loss he never flattered.
translations.idiomatic: He owed the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, deep courtesy; every memorial of profit and loss he sent was free of flattery.

sentences.zh: 子良嘗啓齊武帝論雲爲郡。

translations.literal: Zi Liang once memorialized to Qi Emperor Wu on Yun's service as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang once wrote Qi Emperor Wu recommending Yun for a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「庸人，聞其恒相賣弄，不復窮法，當宥之以遠。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "A mediocrity—I hear he and the prince constantly show off to each other; we need not press the law; let us spare him by sending him far away."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A commonplace fellow—I hear he and the prince forever play to the gallery; no need to pursue the law—send him far off and be done."

sentences.zh: 」子良曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zi Liang said, "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 雲動相規誨，諫書具存，請取以奏。

translations.literal: Yun always counsels and admonishes; his remonstrance letters all survive—please have them brought for memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Yun always advises and remonstrates; the letters remain—let them be submitted."

sentences.zh: 」旣至，有百餘紙，辭皆切直。

translations.literal: When they arrived there were more than a hundred sheets, every word sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: They came to more than a hundred pages, each line blunt and true.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息，因謂子良曰：「不謂雲能爾。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said to Zi Liang, "I did not expect Yun could be like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and told Zi Liang, "I never thought Yun could be such a man.

sentences.zh: 方使弼汝，何宜出守。

translations.literal: He should assist you—why send him out to guard a commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Let him aid you at court—why make him go defend a district?"

sentences.zh: 」齊文惠太子嘗出東田觀獲，顧謂衆賓曰：「刈此亦殊可觀。

translations.literal: Qi's Wenhuai Crown Prince once went to the eastern fields to watch the harvest and said to the guests, "Cutting this too is quite a sight."
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Wenhuai crown prince once went to the eastern estate to watch reaping and told the guests, "This cutting is worth seeing too."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆唯唯。

translations.literal: All murmured agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 雲獨曰：「夫三時之務，實爲長勤。

translations.literal: Yun alone said, "The three seasons' labor is truly long toil.
translations.idiomatic: Yun alone said, "The work of the three seasons is real, lasting labor.

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下知稼穡之艱難，無徇一朝之宴逸。

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness to know the hardship of sowing and reaping and not indulge a single morning's ease."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to know how hard grain is won, and not chase one morning's pleasure."

sentences.zh: 」旣出，侍中蕭緬先不相識，因就車握雲手曰：「不圖今日復聞讜言。

translations.literal: After they left, Attendant Within Xiao Mian, who had not known him before, took his hand at the carriage and said, "I did not expect to hear loyal speech again today."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward attendant within Xiao Mian, a stranger to him before, grasped his hand at the carriage and said, "I never thought to hear honest counsel again today."

sentences.zh: 」及居選官，任守隆重，書牘盈案，賓客滿門，雲應對如流，無所壅滯，官曹文墨，發擿若神，時人咸服其明贍。

translations.literal: When he held the selection office, his posts were weighty; documents piled on his desk and guests filled his gate, yet Yun answered as if flowing water, never blocked; official papers he opened and judged like a spirit—men of the time all admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In charge of appointments his posts were heavy; papers overflowed his desk and guests crowded his door, yet he answered without delay; he sifted official documents with uncanny speed, and all who saw it marveled at his brilliance.

sentences.zh: 性頗激厲，少威重，有所是非，形於造次，士或以此少之。

translations.literal: By nature he was rather sharp and lacked gravitas; when he approved or disapproved he showed it at once—scholars sometimes thought less of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-tempered and light on ceremony; right and wrong showed on his face in the moment, and some gentlemen held that against him.

sentences.zh: 初，雲爲郡號稱廉潔，及居貴重，頗通饋餉；

translations.literal: At first, when Yun held a commandery he was famed for integrity; once he rose to high rank he rather freely accepted gifts;
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he had been famed for clean hands; in high office he accepted presents more freely;

sentences.zh: 然家無蓄積，隨散之親友。

translations.literal: yet his house held no stores, and he gave everything away to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: yet he kept nothing in the house and scattered it all among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he died at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 高祖爲之流涕，卽日輿駕臨殯。

translations.literal: Gaozu wept for him and that same day went in person to his mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept and went himself that very day to the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「追遠興悼，常情所篤；

translations.literal: An edict said, "To pursue the distant and raise lament is feeling men hold deep;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "To honor the departed and mourn is what feeling demands;

sentences.zh: 況問望斯在，事深朝寄者乎！

translations.literal: how much more when reputation still stands and the matter touches the court's trust!"
translations.idiomatic: how much more when renown still lives and the throne leaned on the man!"

sentences.zh: 故散騎常侍、尚書右僕射、霄城侯雲，器範貞正，思懷經遠，爰初立志，素履有聞。

translations.literal: The late Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Xiaocheng Yun—his capacity and bearing were upright, his thought ranged far; from his first resolve his conduct was heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The late regular scattered-cavalry attendant, vice director of the masters of writing, Marquis of Xiaocheng Yun—upright in talent and bearing, far-reaching in mind; from his first vow his walk was known.

sentences.zh: 脫巾來仕，清績仍著。

translations.literal: Removing his scarf to enter service, his clean record still showed.
translations.idiomatic: He doffed the scholar's scarf for office, and his clear record endured.

sentences.zh: 燮務登朝，具瞻惟允。

translations.literal: Harmonizing affairs at court, the gaze of all was granted him.
translations.idiomatic: He balanced court affairs, and every eye trusted him.

sentences.zh: 綢繆翊贊，義簡朕心，雖勤非負靮，而舊同論講。

translations.literal: In close support his righteousness was plain to my heart; though his toil did not wear the traces of the carriage-team, we were old companions in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He wove close support; his loyalty was plain to me—though his labor did not show in the traces of the chariot shaft, we were long friends in counsel.

sentences.zh: 方騁遠塗，永毗庶政；

translations.literal: He was about to run the long road and forever aid common government;
translations.idiomatic: He was to run the long course and forever aid the realm;

sentences.zh: 奄致喪殞，傷悼於懷。

translations.literal: suddenly death came, and grief wounds my breast.
translations.idiomatic: suddenly he fell, and grief cuts my breast.

sentences.zh: 宜加命秩，式備徽典。

translations.literal: Rank and rites should be added to complete the grand precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Let rank and rites be raised to fulfill the great canon.

sentences.zh: 可追贈侍中、衛將軍，僕射、侯如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Attendant Within and Defender General, with Vice Director and Marquis as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously make him attendant within and defender general, vice director and marquis unchanged.

sentences.zh: 並給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Grant also one suite of drums and pipes."
translations.idiomatic: Grant one suite of drums and pipes as well."

sentences.zh: 」禮官請諡曰宣，勑賜諡文。

translations.literal: The ritual officers requested the posthumous name Xuan; an edict bestowed the name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The ritualists proposed posthumous name Xuan; an edict gave Wen.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子孝才嗣，官至太子中舍人。

translations.literal: His son Xiaocai inherited the title and rose to crown prince household aide.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaocai succeeded and reached crown prince household aide.

sentences.zh: 沈約，字休文，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yue, styled Xiucai, was a native of Wukang in Wu-xing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, styled Xiucai, came from Wukang in Wu-xing.

sentences.zh: 祖林子，宋征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Linzi was Song's General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Linzi had been Song's general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 父璞，淮南太守。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pu held Huainan as administrator.

sentences.zh: 璞元嘉末被誅，約幼潛竄，會赦免。

translations.literal: Pu was executed at the end of Yuanjia; Yue as a child went into hiding and was spared by an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's end Pu was put to death; young Yue hid in the shadows until an amnesty let him live.

sentences.zh: 旣而流寓孤貧，篤志好學，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: Then he drifted homeless and poor, set his will on learning, day and night without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered rootless and penniless, fierce in his love of books, never resting from dawn to dark.

sentences.zh: 母恐其以勞生疾，常遣減油滅火。

translations.literal: His mother feared overwork would bring illness and often had him cut lamp oil and put out the fire.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreaded that zeal would break his health and kept sending orders to trim the wick and quench the lamp.

sentences.zh: 而晝之所讀，夜輒誦之，遂博通羣籍，能屬文。

translations.literal: What he read by day he recited by night; he mastered the classics broadly and could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: By day he read, by night he chanted it back until the canon lay open in his mind and his own writing came at will.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 濟陽蔡興宗聞其才而善之；

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong of Jiyang heard of his talent and favored him;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong of Jiyang heard his gift and took to him;

sentences.zh: 興宗爲郢州刺史，引爲安西外兵參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: when Xingzong became Inspector of Yingzhou, he took him as Anxi Outside Army staff officer, also recorder.
translations.idiomatic: when Xingzong took Yingzhou he made him outside-army staff officer to Anxi and recorder as well.

sentences.zh: 興宗嘗謂其諸子曰：「沈記室人倫師表，宜善事之。

translations.literal: Xingzong once told his sons: "Recorder Shen is a model of humanity—treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong once told his sons, "Shen the recorder is a teacher among men—serve him well.

sentences.zh: 」及爲荊州，又爲征西記室參軍，帶厥西令。

translations.literal: " When he went to Jingzhou, he became western campaign recorder, concurrent magistrate of Juesi.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to Jingzhou he became western campaign recorder and magistrate of Juesi in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 興宗卒，始爲安西晉安王法曹參軍，轉外兵，並兼記室。

translations.literal: When Xingzong died, he became Jin'an Wang's legal bureau staff officer, then outside army, both with recorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingzong's death he was legal staff to the Prince of Jin'an, then outside army, always doubling as recorder.

sentences.zh: 入爲尚書度支郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Masters of Writing revenue section attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court as revenue attendant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 齊初爲征虜記室，帶襄陽令，所奉之王，齊文惠太子也。

translations.literal: Early in Qi he was campaign-against-barbarians recorder, concurrent Xiangyang magistrate—the prince he served was Crown Prince Wenhuì.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's opening he was campaign recorder with Xiangyang on his belt—the prince was Crown Prince Wenhuì.

sentences.zh: 太子入居東宮，爲步兵校尉，管書記，直永壽省，校四部圖書。

translations.literal: When the crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace, he was infantry colonel, in charge of records, on duty at Yongshou office, collating the four sections of books.
translations.idiomatic: The heir moved east; he became infantry colonel, keeper of papers, stationed at Yongshou, collating the four library divisions.

sentences.zh: 時東宮多士，約特被親遇，每直入見，影斜方出。

translations.literal: Many scholars were at the Eastern Palace; Yue was specially favored, entering straight through each time and not leaving until his shadow slanted long.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace teemed with talent, yet Yue alone was drawn close—he walked straight in and left only when the sun hung low.

sentences.zh: 當時王侯到宮，或不得進，約每以爲言。

translations.literal: At times princes and marquises coming to the palace could not get in—Yue always spoke up about it.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes even kings and marquises were turned away at the gate, and Yue always pleaded their case.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「吾生平懶起，是卿所悉，得卿談論，然後忘寢。

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "I have been lazy to rise all my life, as you know; only when I talk with you do I forget sleep.
translations.idiomatic: The heir said, "You know how late I like to wake; only your talk makes me forget the bed.

sentences.zh: 卿欲我夙興，可恒早入。

translations.literal: If you want me up early, come in early every day.
translations.idiomatic: If you want me at dawn, come early every day.

sentences.zh: 」遷太子家令，後以本官兼著作郎，遷中書郎，本邑中正，司徒右長史，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Eastern Palace Household Head, later combining that office with Compilation Gentleman, then Secretariat Gentleman, native-district impartial judge, Right Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, and Yellow Gate Gentleman Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to eastern-palace household head, then added compilation gentleman, secretariat gentleman, native impartial judge, right chief of staff to the minister of works, and yellow-gate companion.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵王亦招士，約與蘭陵蕭琛、琅邪王融、陳郡謝朓、南鄉范雲、樂安任昉等皆遊焉，當世號爲得人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling also gathered scholars; Yue with Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langye, Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an, and others all associated—at the time they were called the attained men.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling too kept a salon; Yue moved with Xiao Chen, Wang Rong, Xie Tiao, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, and the rest—men of the age called them the company worth having.

sentences.zh: 俄兼尚書左丞，尋爲御史中丞，轉車騎長史。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, then became Censor-in-Chief, then Chief Clerk of the Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he doubled as left assistant in the Masters of Writing, then censor-in-chief, then chief clerk to the cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，除吏部郎，出爲寧朔將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: In Longchang year 1, he was appointed Department of Personnel Attendant, then went out as Pacify-the-North General and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Longchang year he took the personnel post, then left as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，進號輔國將軍，徵爲五兵尚書，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, his title advanced to Assist-the-State General; he was summoned as Masters of Armaments Minister, then became Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's accession brought him the title assist-the-state; he was called to armaments minister, then made chancellor of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，政歸塚宰，尚書令徐孝嗣使約撰定遺詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, power fell to the chamberlain; Minister Xu Xiaosi had Yue draft the death edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming died the regent held the reins; Xu Xiaosi ordered Yue to fix the final edict.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛將軍，尋加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Guard General, soon with added Unimpeded Transmission Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became left guard general, soon with unimpeded transmission regular attendant added.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，以母老表求解職，改授冠軍將軍、司徒左長史，征虜將軍、南清河太守。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan year 2, citing his mother's age he petitioned to leave office; reassigned as Champion General and Left Chief of Staff of the Minister of Works, Campaign General and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year 2 he begged off for his mother's sake and was shifted to champion general, left chief of staff, campaign general, and administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 高祖在西邸，與約遊舊，建康城平，引爲驃騎司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Gaozu at the Western Residence was an old companion of Yue's; when Jiankang fell peaceful, Yue was made Grand Marshal staff officer, rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu at the western residence knew Yue of old; when Jiankang settled he made him grand-marshal staff officer at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 時高祖勳業旣就，天人允屬，約嘗扣其端，高祖默而不應。

translations.literal: Gaozu's merit was established, heaven and men aligned—Yue once probed the matter; Gaozu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was won and heaven and men agreed; Yue once tested the edge of the question and Gaozu answered with silence.

sentences.zh: 佗日又進曰：「今與古異，不可以淳風期萬物。

translations.literal: Another day he pressed: "Today differs from antiquity—you cannot expect all things by pure custom.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he pressed on: "This age is not the old days—you cannot bind every heart with rustic virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 士大夫攀龍附鳳者，皆望有尺寸之功，以保其福祿。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials who cling to the rising dragon all hope for some small merit to secure fortune and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Every gentleman who rides the dragon's scales wants a scrap of merit to keep his house safe.

sentences.zh: 今童兒牧豎，悉知齊祚已終，莫不云明公其人也。

translations.literal: Now boys and herdboys all know Qi is finished—everyone says you are the man.
translations.idiomatic: Even children at pasture know Qi's mandate is spent and say in one voice that you are the man.

sentences.zh: 天文人事，表革運之徵，永元以來，尤爲彰著。

translations.literal: Astronomy and human affairs show signs of a change of fortune; since Yongyuan this has been especially clear.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs and men's tongues mark the turn of fate—since Yongyuan the proof has glared.

sentences.zh: 讖云『行中水，作天子』，此又歷然在記。

translations.literal: A prophecy says "moving in water, become Son of Heaven"—that too stands plainly in the records.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy runs, "walk midstream and become Son of Heaven"—and the chronicles set it plain.

sentences.zh: 天心不可違，人情不可失，苟是曆數所至，雖欲謙光，亦不可得已。

translations.literal: Heaven's heart may not be defied, human hearts may not be lost—if the succession has arrived, even wishing humility, you cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's will will not be turned aside, nor men's hearts left hanging—when the count of ages has come, modesty cannot hold it back.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「吾方思之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "I am still thinking.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "I am still thinking.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「公初杖兵樊、沔，此時應思，今王業已就，何所復思。

translations.literal: Yue replied: "When you first took arms at Fan and Mian you should have thought; now the royal work is done—what more to think?
translations.idiomatic: Yue answered, "When you first raised arms at Fan and Mian—that was the hour to think. The royal work stands—what is left to think?

sentences.zh: 昔武王伐紂，始入，民便曰吾君，武王不違民意，亦無所思。

translations.literal: When King Wu attacked Zhou and first entered, the people at once called him their lord—Wu did not resist the people's will and had nothing to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu struck Zhou and entered, the people cried "our lord" at once—Wu did not fight the tide and had no second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 公自至京邑，已移氣序，比于周武，遲速不同。

translations.literal: Since you reached the capital the seasons of qi have shifted—compared with King Wu, your pace differs.
translations.idiomatic: From the day you reached the capital the qi of the age has turned—your pace is not King Wu's pace.

sentences.zh: 若不早定大業，稽天人之望，脫有一人立異，便損威德。

translations.literal: If you do not fix the great work early and hold heaven and men waiting, should one man raise a different banner your prestige suffers.
translations.idiomatic: Delay the great settlement and keep heaven and men on the rack—let one man stand apart and your awe is already cut.

sentences.zh: 且人非金石，時事難保。

translations.literal: And men are not metal or stone—times are hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh is not bronze or stone, and the moment is hard to keep.

sentences.zh: 豈可以建安之封，遺之子孫？

translations.literal: Can you leave a mere fief of the Jian'an sort to your sons?
translations.idiomatic: Will you hand your sons only a Jian'an marquisate?

sentences.zh: 若天子還都，公卿在位，則君臣分定，無復異心。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven returns to the capital and dukes and ministers take their posts, lord and subject are fixed and hearts will not turn.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Son of Heaven is back and the great ministers sit in their ranks, lord and servant are set and no heart will wander.

sentences.zh: 君明於上，臣忠於下，豈復有人方更同公作賊。

translations.literal: The ruler clear above, ministers loyal below—who would join you again as a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: A bright lord above, loyal men below—who would rise with you as a rebel again?

sentences.zh: 」高祖然之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu assented.

sentences.zh: 約出，高祖召范雲告之，雲對略同約旨。

translations.literal: Yue left; Gaozu called Fan Yun and told him—Yun's answer matched Yue's gist.
translations.idiomatic: Yue withdrew; Gaozu summoned Fan Yun and told him—Yun's reply tracked Yue's meaning.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「智者乃爾暗同，卿明早將休文更來。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Wise men agree in secret like this—tomorrow bring Xiuwen again early.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Wise men hide the same thought in the dark—bring Xiuwen early tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」雲出語約，約曰：「卿必待我。

translations.literal: Yun went out and told Yue; Yue said: "You must wait for me.
translations.idiomatic: Yun went out and spoke to Yue; Yue said, "You must wait for me.

sentences.zh: 」雲許諾，而約先期入，高祖命草其事。

translations.literal: Yun promised, but Yue entered first and Gaozu ordered him to draft the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yun promised, yet Yue went in ahead; Gaozu told him to draft the business.

sentences.zh: 約乃出懷中詔書並諸選置，高祖初無所改。

translations.literal: Yue produced from his bosom the edict and all appointments—Gaozu changed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue drew from his breast the edict and every appointment; Gaozu altered not a line.

sentences.zh: 俄而雲自外來，至殿門不得入，徘徊壽光閣外，但云「咄咄」。

translations.literal: Soon Yun came from outside; he could not enter the hall door and paced outside Shouguang Pavilion, only crying "Tut tut!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yun arrived from outside, stopped at the hall gate, and paced Shouguang Pavilion crying, "Tsk, tsk!"

sentences.zh: 約出，問曰：「何以見處？

translations.literal: Yue came out; Yun asked how he had been used.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came out; Yun asked, "How were you placed?"

sentences.zh: 」約舉手向左，雲笑曰：「不乖所望。

translations.literal: Yue lifted his hand leftward; Yun laughed: "Not against my hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Yue raised his hand toward the left; Yun laughed, "No betrayal of what I hoped."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，高祖召范雲謂曰：「生平與沈休文羣居，不覺有異人處；

translations.literal: Shortly Gaozu summoned Yun: "Living with Shen Xiuwen, I never felt he was extraordinary;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gaozu called Yun and said, "I lived beside Shen Xiuwen and never felt a strangeness in him;

sentences.zh: 今日才智縱橫，可謂明識。

translations.literal: today his wit runs free—truly clear-sighted."
translations.idiomatic: today his talent runs in every direction—this is true discernment."

sentences.zh: 」雲曰：「公今知約，不異約今知公。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Your Grace now knows Yue—no different from Yue now knowing Your Grace."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "You know Yue now—as Yue already knew you."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「我起兵於今三年矣，功臣諸將，實有其勞，然成帝業者，乃卿二人也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "I have raised arms three years; the meritorious generals have indeed labored—but those who finished the imperial work are you two."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Three years since I took up arms—the captains have their merit, yet the throne was finished by you two alone."

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，爲散騎常侍、吏部尚書，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Liang platform was raised, he was Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Personnel Minister, concurrent Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang terrace rose he was scattered-cavalry regular attendant, personnel minister, and right vice minister together.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，爲尚書僕射，封建昌縣侯，邑千戶，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Gaozu accepted the mandate—Masters of Writing Vice Minister, Marquis of Jianchang, thousand households, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was vice minister of the Masters of Writing, marquis of Jianchang with a thousand households, attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又拜約母謝爲建昌國太夫人。

translations.literal: Yue's mother Lady Xie was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jianchang state.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's mother, Lady Xie, was made grand lady of Jianchang state.

sentences.zh: 奉策之日，右僕射范雲等二十餘人咸來致拜，朝野以爲榮。

translations.literal: On the day of receiving the patent, Vice Minister Fan Yun and more than twenty others all came to bow—court and country took it for glory.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the patent was received, Fan Yun the vice minister and twenty-odd others all came to bow—court and market called it glory.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書左僕射，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Left Vice Minister, attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was left vice minister, attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 尋兼領軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon concurrent command of the guards, added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded the guards in addition and gained palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，遭母憂，輿駕親出臨弔，以約年衰，不宜致毀，遣中書舍人斷客節哭。

translations.literal: Tianjian year 2, mourning mother—the emperor came in person to console; considering Yue's age, excessive grief was unsuitable; sent a Secretariat staffer to stop visitors and regulate weeping.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 2 he mourned his mother; the emperor came out in person to condole, judged Yue too old for ruinous grief, and sent a secretariat aide to cut off guests and set bounds to the wailing.

sentences.zh: 起爲鎮軍將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。

translations.literal: He returned to office as Suppressing Army General and Intendant of Danyang with full staff.
translations.idiomatic: He left mourning as suppressing-army general and intendant of Danyang, with a full staff appointed.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷侍中、右光祿大夫，領太子詹事，揚州大中正，關尚書八條事，遷尚書令，侍中、詹事、中正如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended: Palace Attendant, Right Grandee, Eastern Palace Tutor, Yangzhou chief impartial judge, oversight of eight Masters items, then Masters Minister—attendant, tutor, judge unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning ended he was palace attendant, right grandee, eastern-palace tutor, Yangzhou chief impartial judge, charged with eight secretariat matters, then minister of the Masters of Writing—attendant, tutor, and judge unchanged.

sentences.zh: 累表陳讓，改授尚書左僕射、領中書令、前將軍，置佐史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Repeated memorials to decline; reassigned Left Vice Minister, concurrent Secretariat Director, Front General, with staff, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again and again to yield; they made him left vice minister with secretariat director, front general, staff, and attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書令，領太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon Masters Minister, concurrent Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor to the heir together.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉左光祿大夫，侍中、少傅如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Year 9: Left Grandee, attendant and junior tutor as before, one set of martial pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he became left grandee, attendant and junior tutor unchanged, with one set of martial pipes.

sentences.zh: 初，約久處端揆，有志台司，論者咸謂爲宜，而帝終不用，乃求外出，又不見許。

translations.literal: Long at the peak of government, he aimed at the tripod-post; observers said it fit—the emperor never used him; he sought to go out, was refused.
translations.idiomatic: He had long stood at the summit and coveted the highest seat; men said it was fitting, yet the emperor never gave it—he asked to go out and was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 與徐勉素善，遂以書陳情於勉曰：「吾弱年孤苦，傍無朞屬，往者將墜於地，契闊屯邅，困於朝夕，崎嶇薄宦，事非爲己，望得小祿，傍此東歸。

translations.literal: He was close to Xu Mian and wrote to lay bare his heart: "In my weak years I was orphaned and alone, with no kin near; once I was about to fall to earth—through hardship and peril, trapped morning and evening, climbing rough steps in petty office not for myself, hoping for a small stipend to settle near home in the east.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Xu Mian and wrote to open his heart: "In tender years I was orphaned, with no kin at hand; I nearly fell to the ground—years of want and danger, squeezed morning and night, climbing petty posts I did not want, only to win a small salary and live out my days near home in the east.

sentences.zh: 歲逾十稔，方忝襄陽縣，公私情計，非所了具，以身資物，不得不任人事。

translations.literal: More than ten years passed before I was honored with Xiangyang county—public and private accounts I could not clear, and with my person as collateral I could not refuse human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years passed before I barely held Xiangyang county; public and private ledgers I could not square, and my body was the pledge—I could not refuse the world's business.

sentences.zh: 永明末，出守東陽，意在止足；

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming I went out to guard Dongyang, my heart set on stopping;
translations.idiomatic: At Yongming's end I went out to Dongyang, my heart already on stopping;

sentences.zh: 而建武肇運，人世膠加，一去不返，行之未易。

translations.literal: but Jianwu opened a new fortune and the world glued itself tighter—one departure does not return, and the walking is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: then Jianwu opened a new reign and the world clung tighter—one step out does not come back, and the road is not easy.

sentences.zh: 及昏猜之始，王政多門，因此謀退，庶幾可果，託卿布懷於徐令，想記未忘。

translations.literal: When dim suspicion began and royal affairs had many doors, I plotted to withdraw, hoping it might succeed—I entrusted my mind to you to lay before Supervisor Xu, thinking the record is not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne turned dim and many hands held the reins, I schemed to withdraw, hoping it might succeed—I asked you to carry my wish to Supervisor Xu, trusting you had not forgotten.

sentences.zh: 聖道聿興，謬逢嘉運，往志宿心，復成乖爽。

translations.literal: When the holy way rose up I wrongly met a fine season; old will and long intent became wrong again.
translations.idiomatic: When the holy way rose I stumbled into a bright season, and the will I nursed for years turned false again.

sentences.zh: 今歲開元，禮年云至，懸車之請，事由恩奪。

translations.literal: This year Kaiyuan—the ritual year arrives—the request to hang up the chariot is denied by grace.
translations.idiomatic: This Kaiyuan year the ritual clock says my turn—the plea to hang up the chariot is denied by grace.

sentences.zh: 誠不能弘宣風政，光闡朝猷，尚欲討尋文簿，時議同異。

translations.literal: Truly I cannot spread wind-policies or brighten court plans; I still wish to examine registers and seasonal debate.
translations.idiomatic: I truly cannot widen the wind of government or light the court's counsel; I still mean to comb the archives and weigh what men say.

sentences.zh: 而開年以來，病增慮切，當由生靈有限，勞役過差，總此凋竭，歸之暮年，牽策行止，努力祗事。

translations.literal: But since the year opened illness and worry grew—perhaps because life has limits and labor exceeded measure—gathering this exhaustion to my age, I drive my steps and force the service.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the year turned, sickness and dread have grown—perhaps life has a measure and labor passed it—this wasting gathers on my old bones, and I whip my steps to barely serve.

sentences.zh: 外觀傍覽，尚似全人，而形骸力用，不相綜攝，常須過自束持，方可僶勉。

translations.literal: To outside eyes I still look whole, but form and strength do not coordinate; I must always bind myself tight to barely manage.
translations.idiomatic: From outside I still seem a whole man, yet body and force no longer answer each other; I must brace myself every hour to scrape through.

sentences.zh: 解衣一臥，支體不復相關。

translations.literal: Undo my robes and lie down—limbs no longer answer each other.
translations.idiomatic: Strip off my robe and lie down—my limbs no longer heed one another.

sentences.zh: 上熱下冷，月增日篤，取暖則煩，加寒必利，後差不及前差，後劇必甚前劇。

translations.literal: Heat above, cold below, month by month worse—warmth brings trouble, cold brings relief, each bout weaker than the last, each crisis sharper than the one before.
translations.idiomatic: Heat above, cold below, worse with every moon—warmth vexes me, cold steadies me, each spell weaker than the last, each turn sharper than the one before.

sentences.zh: 百日數旬，革帶常應移孔；

translations.literal: For days and decades the belt must move a hole;
translations.idiomatic: In spans of days and decades the belt must shift a notch;

sentences.zh: 以手握臂，率計月小半分。

translations.literal: grasp the arm with the hand—each month a little less by half a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: close my hand on my arm—each month a little less by half a measure.

sentences.zh: 以此推算，豈能支久？

translations.literal: By this reckoning how can I last long?
translations.idiomatic: Count it so—how can I last?

sentences.zh: 若此不休，日復一日，將貽聖主不追之恨。

translations.literal: If this does not stop, day piled on day, it will leave the sage lord unappeasable regret.
translations.idiomatic: If this does not end, day on day, it will leave our sage lord a regret that cannot be soothed.

sentences.zh: 冒欲表聞，乞歸老之秩。

translations.literal: I dare wish to memorialize and beg the rank of return in old age.
translations.idiomatic: I dare memorialize and beg the rank of withdrawal in old age.

sentences.zh: 若天假其年，還是平健，才力所堪，惟思是策。

translations.literal: If Heaven lends years and I return to fair health, what strength allows—that is the only plan I ponder."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants years and I return to sound health, whatever strength remains—that alone is the plan I keep."

sentences.zh: 」勉爲言於高祖，請三司之儀，弗許，但加鼓吹而已。

translations.literal: Mian spoke to Gaozu; asked for three-office ritual—refused, only added pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Mian spoke for him to Gaozu and asked the rites of the three offices—refused; only the pipes were added.

sentences.zh: 約性不飲酒，少嗜欲，雖時遇隆重，而居處儉素。

translations.literal: By nature Yue did not drink and had few desires; though honors piled up, his dwelling stayed spare.
translations.idiomatic: Yue did not drink by nature and wanted little; though rank piled on him, his house stayed plain.

sentences.zh: 立宅東田，矚望郊阜。

translations.literal: He built a house on the eastern fields, gazing out over the suburban hills.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house in the eastern fields and looked out over the suburban slopes.

sentences.zh: 嘗爲《郊居賦》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: He once composed the "Fu of Suburban Living"; its words run:
translations.idiomatic: Once he wrote the "Fu of Suburban Living"; it begins:

sentences.zh: 惟至人之非己，固物我而兼忘。

translations.literal: Only the perfected man forgets self, firmly forgetting self and things together.
translations.idiomatic: The perfected man forgets himself and holds self and world in one forgetting.

sentences.zh: 自中智以下洎，咸得性以爲場。

translations.literal: From middling wisdom downward, all take nature as their field.
translations.idiomatic: Below middling wit, every creature takes its nature for its pasture.

sentences.zh: 獸因窟而獲騁，鳥先巢而後翔。

translations.literal: Beasts run free because they have dens; birds nest first, then soar.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts stretch their legs because they have burrows; birds build the nest, then take the sky.

sentences.zh: 陳巷窮而業泰，嬰居湫而德昌。

translations.literal: Chen's alleys ended poor yet his work flourished; Ying dwelt cramped yet his virtue shone.
translations.idiomatic: Chen lived in a dead-end lane yet his house rose; Ying kept a mean roof yet his virtue widened.

sentences.zh: 僑棲仁於東里，鳳晦跡於西堂。

translations.literal: Qiao lodged his benevolence in the eastern lane; the phoenix hid its tracks in the western hall.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao planted benevolence in the eastern lane; the phoenix veiled its steps in the western hall.

sentences.zh: 伊吾人之褊志，無經世之大方。

translations.literal: My own will is narrow; I have no great plan for the age.
translations.idiomatic: My will is small; I own no grand design for the world.

sentences.zh: 思依林而羽戢，願託水而鱗藏。

translations.literal: I would fold my wings to the woods and sheath my scales in the water.
translations.idiomatic: I would fold my wings to the forest and hide my scales in the stream.

sentences.zh: 固無情於輪奐，非有欲於康莊。

translations.literal: I have no love for painted beams, no craving for the broad road.
translations.idiomatic: I do not hunger for carved rafters, nor thirst for the king's highway.

sentences.zh: 披東郊之寥廓，入蓬藋之荒茫。

translations.literal: I open the eastern suburbs' wide silence and enter the wild tangle of reeds and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: I push into the eastern outskirts' emptiness and walk the waste of reed and rush.

sentences.zh: 旣從豎而橫構，亦風除而雨攘。

translations.literal: Already it stood crosswise and lengthwise; wind had stripped it and rain had scattered it.
translations.idiomatic: It had been built out and across; wind cleared it and rain tore it down.

sentences.zh: 昔西漢之標季，余播遷之雲始。

translations.literal: In Western Han's declining age, my wandering began when the clouds first gathered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twilight of Western Han, my exile began at the clouded dawn.

sentences.zh: 違利建於海昏，創惟桑于江汜。

translations.literal: We left Lizhou's seat at Haihun and planted mulberry on the Jiang ford.
translations.idiomatic: We forsook Haihun's prosperous seat and set mulberry on the river's edge.

sentences.zh: 同河濟之重世，逾班生之十紀。

translations.literal: Like the Huang and Ji basin through heavy generations, we passed beyond Ban's ten epochs.
translations.idiomatic: We shared the Yellow and Ji country's long ages and outlived Ban's ten generations.

sentences.zh: 或辭祿而反耕，或彈冠而來仕。

translations.literal: Some refused salary and returned to the plow; some dusted their caps and came to office.
translations.idiomatic: Some turned down rank and went back to the fields; some shook off dust and entered service.

sentences.zh: 逮有晉之隆安，集艱虞于天步。

translations.literal: Then came Jin's Long'an prosperity, gathering hardship and peril at heaven's pace.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jin's Long'an gathered trial and trouble into the march of days.

sentences.zh: 世交爭而波流，民失時而狼顧。

translations.literal: Ages clashed in tumbling waves; the people lost their season and glanced back like wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Generations fought in rolling surf; men lost their hour and looked over their shoulders like wolves.

sentences.zh: 延亂麻于井邑，曝如莽于衢路。

translations.literal: Chaos's hemp stretched over towns and hamlets; ruin like wild grass blazed along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Disorder's tangle covered market and lane; waste like rank weeds burned on every road.

sentences.zh: 大地曠而靡容，旻天遠而誰訴。

translations.literal: The great earth lay empty with no room for a man; the distant sky was far—who would hear my plea?
translations.idiomatic: The wide land had no place left for a body; the high heaven was remote—who could I call?

sentences.zh: 伊皇祖之弱辰，逢時艱之孔棘。

translations.literal: In my imperial ancestor's feeble years, the season's hardship pressed sharp as a thorn.
translations.idiomatic: In the soft years of my royal forebear, the times' trouble came close as a barb.

sentences.zh: 違危邦而窘驚，訪安土而移卽。

translations.literal: Fleeing the perilous state in alarm, he sought a safe land and moved to settle.
translations.idiomatic: He fled a realm in danger, sought a gentler country, and went to make his home.

sentences.zh: 肇胥宇於朱方，掩閒庭而晏息。

translations.literal: First he found shelter at Zhufang, closing the quiet courtyard to rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He first took roof at Zhufang, shut the still court, and slept untroubled.

sentences.zh: 值龍顏之鬱起，乃憑風而矯翼。

translations.literal: When the dragon countenance rose in splendor, then on wind he spread his correcting wings.
translations.idiomatic: When the dragon face lifted in glory, he rode the wind and straightened his wings.

sentences.zh: 指皇邑而南轅，駕脩衢以騁力。

translations.literal: He aimed the carriage yoke at the imperial city and drove south; he harnessed the broad highway to exert his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the yoke toward the royal capital and went south; he took the great road and put his strength to use.

sentences.zh: 遷華扉而來啓，張高衡而徙植。

translations.literal: He moved the splendid gates and came to open them; he raised the high beam and transplanted it.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted the bright doors and came to set them wide; he lifted the tall ridgepole and set it anew.

sentences.zh: 傍逸陌之脩平，面淮流之清直。

translations.literal: Beside the leisure avenues' smooth expanse, facing the Huai's current clear and straight.
translations.idiomatic: By the level paths of the outer lanes, before the Huai's clear, straight flow.

sentences.zh: 芳塵浸而悠遠，世道忽其窊隆。

translations.literal: Fragrant dust soaked ever farther off; the world's way suddenly rose and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Perfumed dust steeped the distance; the age's road pitched up and down.

sentences.zh: 綿四代於茲日，盈百祀於微躬。

translations.literal: Four generations stretch down to this day; a hundred sacrificial years upon my humble person.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations run to this morning; a hundred rites weigh on my slight life.

sentences.zh: 嗟弊廬之難保，若霣籜之從風。

translations.literal: Alas for the ruined cottage hard to keep, like rain-broken bamboo swept by the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Ah—the broken lodge that will not stand, like split bamboo driven by the gale.

sentences.zh: 或誅茅而剪棘，或旣西而復東。

translations.literal: Some cut thatch and pruned thorns anew; some had gone west and returned east again.
translations.idiomatic: Some mended the roof and cleared the thorns; some went west, then came back east.

sentences.zh: 乍容身於白社，亦寄孥於伯通。

translations.literal: Now sheltering in the White Shrine, now entrusting wife and children to Bo Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Now hiding in the White Shrine, now lodging kin with Bo Tong.

sentences.zh: 迹平生之耿介，實有心於獨往。

translations.literal: The traces of my life's upright integrity—truly I kept a heart that walked alone.
translations.idiomatic: The track of my days was straight and hard; I meant to keep a heart that went alone.

sentences.zh: 思幽人而軫念，望東臯而長想。

translations.literal: I thought of the reclusive man and felt deep pity; I gazed at the eastern ridge and longed.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned the man apart from the world and turned my eyes to the eastern terrace in longing.

sentences.zh: 本忘情於徇物，徒羈絏於天壤。

translations.literal: By nature I had forgotten feeling for outer things, only to be bound by heaven's dust.
translations.idiomatic: I was born to forget the world's goods, yet only wound in heaven's dust.

sentences.zh: 應屢歎於牽絲，陸興言於世網。

translations.literal: Ying Pu-ke sighed again and again at threads that pulled; Lu Ji spoke of the world's net.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Pu-ke groaned at every tug of thread; Lu Ji named the net the age weaves.

sentences.zh: 事滔滔而未合，志悁悁而無爽。

translations.literal: Affairs ran on, ungathered; my will was anxious yet never lost its integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Business poured on without rest; my heart was tight but never bent.

sentences.zh: 路將殫而彌峭，情薄暮而踰廣。

translations.literal: The road neared its end and grew steeper still; feeling at dusk spread ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: The path was nearly spent and grew sharper; at evening my longing widened.

sentences.zh: 抱寸心其如蘭，何斯願之浩蕩。

translations.literal: I held an inch of heart fragrant as orchids—how vast this longing's flood!
translations.idiomatic: I carried a span of heart sweet as orchid—how wide this wish runs!

sentences.zh: 詠歸歟而躑跼，眷岩阿而抵掌。

translations.literal: I chanted "Returning!" yet stood rooted in place; I looked toward the rocky crags and clapped my hands.
translations.idiomatic: I sang of going home yet could not move; I turned to the cliff and struck my palms.

sentences.zh: 逢時君之喪德，何凶昏之孔熾。

translations.literal: I met a lord who had lost virtue; how deep the wicked darkness burned!
translations.idiomatic: I met a ruler without virtue; how thick the evil night burned!

sentences.zh: 乃戰牧所未陳，實升陑所不記。

translations.literal: Battles at Muye were never arrayed such as this; feats at Mount Sheng were not set down in records.
translations.idiomatic: No battle at Muye was ever fought like this; no deed at Mount Sheng was ever written in the books.

sentences.zh: 彼黎元之喋喋，將垂獸而爲餌。

translations.literal: The common people chattered—they would soon be fed to beasts as bait.
translations.idiomatic: The people murmured—they would soon be meat hung out for beasts.

sentences.zh: 瞻穹昊而無歸，雖非牢而被胾。

translations.literal: They looked up at the round sky and had no refuge; though not in the pen, they were meat on the block.
translations.idiomatic: They stared at the round heaven and had nowhere to turn; though not yet in the stall, they were already flesh on the board.

sentences.zh: 始歎絲而未睹，終逌組而後值。

translations.literal: At first I sighed at the threads and saw no way through; at last I met the prime minister who opened the web.
translations.idiomatic: First I grieved at the snarl and saw no end; at last I met the chief minister who cut the threads.

sentences.zh: 尋貽愛乎上天，固非民其莫甚。

translations.literal: I found grace bestowed from above on high—surely no people were more sorely tried.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's kindness reached down—surely no folk had suffered more.

sentences.zh: 授冥符於井翼，實靈命之所稟。

translations.literal: The dark tally was granted at the Well and Wings constellations—truly the numinous mandate was received.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden token came at the Well and Wings—truly the bright charge was taken.

sentences.zh: 當降監之初辰，值積惡之云稔。

translations.literal: At the season when heaven lowered its watch, the piled evil ripened like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven first bent its gaze, long-stored wrong ripened like thundercloud.

sentences.zh: 寧方割於下墊，廓重氛於上墋。

translations.literal: Though the lower realm was carved into regions, the heavy miasma was cleared from the upper vault.
translations.idiomatic: Though the lower land was cut into parts, the thick haze was swept from the high dome.

sentences.zh: 躬靡暇於朝食，常求衣於夜枕。

translations.literal: He himself had no leisure for the morning meal; he often sought his garment at the night's pillow.
translations.idiomatic: He had no time even to eat at dawn; he often looked for his robe on the night pillow.

sentences.zh: 旣牢籠于媯、夏，又驅馳乎軒、頊。

translations.literal: Already he had caged the dynasties of Yao and Xia; again he drove the eras of Xuan and Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had already bound the lines of Yao and Xia; again he drove the reigns of Xuan and Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 德無遠而不被，明無微而不燭。

translations.literal: Virtue reached where no place was remote; illumination spared not the smallest flicker.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue went where no land was far; his light left no corner unlit.

sentences.zh: 鼓玄澤於大荒，播仁風於遐俗。

translations.literal: He beat the dark marsh across the great waste; he sowed humane winds through distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: He drummed the deep fen across the wild; he scattered humane wind through far-off custom.

sentences.zh: 辟終古而遐念，信王猷其如玉。

translations.literal: From the remotest antiquity he turned his far thought—truly the royal plan was jade.
translations.idiomatic: He looked back through deepest time—truly the king's design was jade.

sentences.zh: 值銜《圖》之盛世，遇興聖之嘉期。

translations.literal: He met an age when the River Chart was held in the mouth; he encountered the season when a sagely rise was blessed.
translations.idiomatic: He came to a time when the River Chart was in hand; he met the hour when a holy rise was praised.

sentences.zh: 謝中涓於初日，叨光佐於此時。

translations.literal: I left the inner attendant's post on the first day and received the light of a supporting minister in this hour.
translations.idiomatic: I quit the inner attendant on the first day and took the bright post of a helping minister in this season.

sentences.zh: 闕投石之猛志，無飛矢之麗辭。

translations.literal: I lacked the fierce will to cast stones; I had no splendid words of flying arrow-phrases.
translations.idiomatic: I had no heart to cast the stone; I had no shining speech of the flying arrow.

sentences.zh: 排陽鳥而命邑，方河山而啓基。

translations.literal: I drove off the sun-bird and was ordered a district; I squared the mountains and rivers and opened the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: I drove away the sun-bird and was given a town; I set the mountains and rivers in order and laid the base.

sentences.zh: 翼儲光於三善，長王職於百司。

translations.literal: I aided the stored light of the three excellences and long held royal duty among the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: I helped the stored light of the three virtues and long kept royal work among the hundred bureaus.

sentences.zh: 兢鄙夫之易失，懼寵祿之難持。

translations.literal: I trembled at the vulgar man's easy loss; I feared favor and salary were hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: I feared how quickly the common man loses his hold; I dreaded how hard rank and pay are to keep.

sentences.zh: 伊前世之貴仕，罕紆情於丘窟。

translations.literal: In former ages the honored officials—how rarely they bent their hearts to hill and cave!
translations.idiomatic: In old days the great ministers—how seldom they bowed their hearts to hill and hollow!

sentences.zh: 譬叢華於楚、趙，每驕奢以相越。

translations.literal: Like clustered glory in Chu and Zhao, each drove pride and extravagance beyond the next.
translations.idiomatic: Like flowers massed in Chu and Zhao, each outdid the last in pride and waste.

sentences.zh: 築甲館於銅駝，並高門於北闕。

translations.literal: They built armored halls at the Bronze Camel; they stacked high gates at the northern tower.
translations.idiomatic: They raised armored lodges at the Bronze Camel; they piled tall gates at the northern watch.

sentences.zh: 辟重扃于華閫，豈蓬蒿所能沒。

translations.literal: Heavy gates opened on the flower ward—how could wild mugwort bury them?
translations.idiomatic: Great doors opened on the flowered ward—how could mere mugwort cover them?

sentences.zh: 敖傳嗣於墝壤，何安身於窮地。

translations.literal: Proud Ao left his line on broken ground—how could one settle body in a straitened place?
translations.idiomatic: Proud Ao's heirs lived on broken soil—how could a man find rest in a narrow land?

sentences.zh: 味先哲而爲言，固余心之所嗜。

translations.literal: I take the former sages' words for my own speech—truly my heart's taste alone delights.
translations.idiomatic: I make the old wise men's sayings my tongue—only what my heart loves pleases me.

sentences.zh: 不慕權於城市，豈邀名於屠肆。

translations.literal: I do not admire power in the market city; I do not beg fame in the butcher's lane.
translations.idiomatic: I do not crave power in the market streets; I do not hunt name in the butcher's row.

sentences.zh: 詠希微以考室，幸風霜之可庇。

translations.literal: I chant the rare and subtle to shape my chamber; good fortune that wind and frost may shelter me.
translations.idiomatic: I sing the hidden and fine to build my room; luck that wind and frost can roof me.

sentences.zh: 爾乃傍窮野，抵荒郊；

translations.literal: Thus I came beside the forsaken wilds, reaching the waste outskirts;
translations.idiomatic: So I came by the empty wild, to the bare edge of the suburbs;

sentences.zh: 編霜菼，葺寒茅。

translations.literal: I plaited frost-reed and patched the cold thatch.
translations.idiomatic: I wove frost-reed and mended the winter roof.

sentences.zh: 構棲噪之所集，築町疃之所交。

translations.literal: I built a perch where clamor gathered, laid out strips where field paths met.
translations.idiomatic: I made a roost where noise would settle, traced plots where field tracks crossed.

sentences.zh: 因犯簷而刊樹，由妨基而剪巢。

translations.literal: Because eaves offended, I cut the trees; because the base would suffer, I trimmed the nests.
translations.idiomatic: Where the eaves were blocked, I felled trees; where the footings would fail, I cleared nests.

sentences.zh: 決渟洿之汀濙，塞井甃之淪坳。

translations.literal: I opened the stagnant pool's shallow backwater; I blocked the well tile's sunken hollow.
translations.idiomatic: I cut the still pond's shallow rim; I filled the well curb's fallen dip.

sentences.zh: 藝芳枳於北渠，樹脩楊於南浦。

translations.literal: I planted fragrant trifoliate on the north ditch, set tall poplars on the south ford.
translations.idiomatic: I set sweet orange on the north ditch, tall poplar on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 遷甕牖於蘭室，同肩牆於華堵。

translations.literal: I moved the pottery window into the orchid room; the shared shoulder-wall matched a splendid rampart.
translations.idiomatic: I brought the clay window into the orchid chamber; the shared wall stood like a bright fortress.

sentences.zh: 織宿楚以成門，籍外扉而爲戶。

translations.literal: I wove overnight rushes for a gate, took the outer leaf-boards for doors.
translations.idiomatic: I bound last night's rushes into a gate, took outer boards for doors.

sentences.zh: 旣取陰於庭樾，又因籬于芳杜。

translations.literal: I already took shade from the courtyard's shade trees, and relied on the hedge of fragrant elm.
translations.idiomatic: I took shade from the court trees, and leaned on a hedge of sweet elm.

sentences.zh: 開閣室以遠臨，辟高軒而旁睹。

translations.literal: I opened the inner chamber for a far prospect; I cleared the high hall's side view.
translations.idiomatic: I opened the inner room to look far off; I widened the high hall to see aside.

sentences.zh: 漸沼沚於霤垂，周塍陌於堂下。

translations.literal: The marsh islet soaked in at the eaves' drip; the field paths ringed the hall below.
translations.idiomatic: The marsh edge crept under the dripping eaves; field paths circled the hall below.

sentences.zh: 其水草則蘋萍芡芰，菁藻蒹菰；

translations.literal: Of water plants—duckweed, water-shield, gorgon, lotus, duckweed, reed, rush;
translations.idiomatic: For water growth—duckweed, shield-plant, gorgon, lotus, duckweed, reed, rush;

sentences.zh: 石衣海髮，黃荇綠蒲。

translations.literal: stone moss, sea tresses, yellow pondweed, green cattail.
translations.idiomatic: stone moss, sea hair, yellow pondweed, green cattail.

sentences.zh: 動紅荷於輕浪，覆碧葉於澄湖。

translations.literal: Red lotus stirred on light ripples; green leaves covered the clear lake.
translations.idiomatic: Red lotus moved on soft waves; green leaf roofed the clear mere.

sentences.zh: 飡嘉實而卻老，振羽服於清都。

translations.literal: We ate fine fruit to push off age; we shook feather robes in the pure capital.
translations.idiomatic: We ate good fruit to turn back age; we shook feather coats in the clean court.

sentences.zh: 其陸卉則紫鼈綠葹，天著山韭；

translations.literal: Of land plants—purple turtle, green sprout, sky thistle, mountain chive;
translations.idiomatic: For land herbs—purple turtle, green sprout, sky thistle, mountain chive;

sentences.zh: 雁齒麋舌，牛脣彘首。

translations.literal: goose-tooth, elk-tongue, ox-lip, pig-head.
translations.idiomatic: goose tooth, elk tongue, ox lip, pig head.

sentences.zh: 布濩南池之陽，爛漫北樓之後。

translations.literal: Spread on the south pond's sunny bank, riotous behind the north tower.
translations.idiomatic: They spread on the south pool's bright side, ran wild behind the north lodge.

sentences.zh: 或幕渚而芘地，或縈窗而窺牖。

translations.literal: Some shaded the islet and roofed the ground; some threaded the window to peep at the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Some roofed the islet and covered the earth; some laced the window to look through the frame.

sentences.zh: 若乃園宅殊制，田圃異區。

translations.literal: Then gardens and dwellings had special forms; fields and orchards different zones.
translations.idiomatic: Then garden and house had their own shapes; field and orchard their own plots.

sentences.zh: 李衡則橘林千樹，石崇則雜果萬株。

translations.literal: Li Heng had a thousand orange trees; Shi Chong had ten thousand mixed fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng kept a thousand orange trees; Shi Chong ten thousand mixed fruits.

sentences.zh: 並豪情之所侈，非儉志之所娛。

translations.literal: Both were what proud spirit loved to display—not what a frugal will took for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Both were what bold hearts loved to show—not what a spare heart took for joy.

sentences.zh: 欲令紛披蓊鬱，吐綠攢朱；

translations.literal: I wanted them thick and lush, pouring green and heaped crimson;
translations.idiomatic: I wished them rank and thick, green poured out and red piled high;

sentences.zh: 羅窗映戶，接溜承隅。

translations.literal: latticing windows, reflecting doors, linked eaves meeting corners.
translations.idiomatic: latticed windows, mirrored doors, joined eaves at every corner.

sentences.zh: 開丹房以四照，舒翠葉而九衢。

translations.literal: Opening crimson chambers on four sides, spreading jade leaves on nine crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson rooms opened to four lights; jade leaves spread on nine ways.

sentences.zh: 抽紅英於紫帶，銜素蕊於青跗。

translations.literal: Drawing red blossoms from purple sashes, holding white stamens on green calyxes.
translations.idiomatic: Red bloom drawn from purple bands; white stamen held on green calyx.

sentences.zh: 其林鳥則翻泊頡頏，遺音下上；

translations.literal: Of forest birds—darting, resting, nodding, leaving sound above and below;
translations.idiomatic: For birds of the wood—wheeling, settling, dipping, leaving cry above and below;

sentences.zh: 楚雀多名，流嚶雜響。
