translations.literal: Chu sparrows of many names, flowing warbles in mixed choruses.
translations.idiomatic: Chu finches of many names, flowing song in mixed chorus.

sentences.zh: 或班尾而綺翼，或綠衿而絳顙。

translations.literal: Some with patterned tails and brocade wings, some with green collars and scarlet crowns.
translations.idiomatic: Some with brocade tail and patterned wing, some with green neck and red brow.

sentences.zh: 好葉隱而枝藏，乍間關而來往。

translations.literal: They loved hidden leaves and concealed branches, now and then crossing with calls in passage.
translations.idiomatic: They loved hidden leaf and covered branch, now and then calling as they crossed.

sentences.zh: 其水禽則大鴻小雁，天狗澤虞；

translations.literal: Of water birds—great swan and small goose, celestial hound and marsh guardian;
translations.idiomatic: For water fowl—great swan and small goose, sky hound and marsh keeper;

sentences.zh: 秋鷖寒＜勑鳥＞，修鷁短鳧。

translations.literal: autumn egret, winter gull, long egret, short teal.
translations.idiomatic: autumn heron, winter gull, long egret, short duck.

sentences.zh: 曳參差之弱藻，戲瀺灂之輕軀；

translations.literal: trailing uneven frail weeds, playing their light bodies in the shallows;
translations.idiomatic: dragging uneven soft weed, sporting light bodies in the shallows;

sentences.zh: 翅抨流而起沫，翼鼓浪而成珠。

translations.literal: wings beat the stream and lifted foam, wings stirred waves into pearls.
translations.idiomatic: wings struck the flow and raised foam, wings ruffled the wave into pearls.

sentences.zh: 其魚則赤鯉青魴，纖倏鉅鱯。

translations.literal: Of fish—red carp and green bream, slender minnow and great catfish.
translations.idiomatic: For fish—red carp and green bream, thin dart and heavy catfish.

sentences.zh: 碧鱗朱尾，脩顱偃額。

translations.literal: jade scales and cinnabar tails, long heads and flat brows.
translations.idiomatic: jade scale and cinnabar tail, long head and flat brow.

sentences.zh: 小則戲渚成文，大則噴流揚白。

translations.literal: small ones patterned the shallows in play; great ones spewed the current in white spray.
translations.idiomatic: small ones wrote patterns on the shoal; great ones threw white spray from the stream.

sentences.zh: 不興羨於江海，聊相忘於余宅。

translations.literal: I do not envy river and sea; for now we forget each other in my dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: I do not envy the river and the sea; for now we only forget each other in my house.

sentences.zh: 其竹則東南獨秀，九府擅奇。

translations.literal: Of bamboo—the southeast's lone excellence, nine prefectures' special wonder.
translations.idiomatic: For bamboo—the southeast's single glory, the nine offices' own marvel.

sentences.zh: 不遷植於淇水，豈分根於樂池。

translations.literal: Not transplanted from the Qi waters; how could roots be divided at the music pool?
translations.idiomatic: Not moved from the Qi river; how could roots be split at the music pool?

sentences.zh: 秋蜩吟葉，寒雀噪枝。

translations.literal: Autumn cicadas sang on the leaves; winter sparrows clamored on the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn cicada sang on the leaf; winter sparrow cried on the branch.

sentences.zh: 來風南軒之下，負雪北堂之垂。

translations.literal: Wind came to the south study's eaves; snow pressed the north hall's fringe.
translations.idiomatic: Wind reached the south study's eaves; snow weighed the north hall's edge.

sentences.zh: 訪往塗之軫跡，觀先識之情偽。

translations.literal: I visited past roads' turning traces; I watched earlier men's true and false.
translations.idiomatic: I walked the old road's wheel tracks; I watched how the men before judged true and false.

sentences.zh: 每誅空而索有，皆指難以爲易。

translations.literal: Each time they condemn emptiness yet demand substance, all point at what is hard and call it easy.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again they rail at the void and hunt for substance, calling every hardship easy.

sentences.zh: 不自已而求足，並尤物以興累。

translations.literal: Not content with themselves yet seeking fullness, together they blame things for raising burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Unsatisfied in themselves yet greedy for more, they heap blame on things and call it burden.

sentences.zh: 亦昔士之所迷，而今余之所避也。

translations.literal: What past gentlemen were lost in is what I now avoid.
translations.idiomatic: The maze that trapped men of old is the path I turn from today.

sentences.zh: 原農皇之攸始，討厥播之云初。

translations.literal: I trace to where the Divine Farmer first began, inquire into the cloud-origins of sowing.
translations.idiomatic: I reach back to where the Divine Farmer began and ask how the first seeding rose from cloud.

sentences.zh: 肇變腥以粒食，乃人命之所儲。

translations.literal: When raw flesh turned to grain for food—that was what human life stored up.
translations.idiomatic: When blood and raw meat became grain—that was the storehouse of human life.

sentences.zh: 尋井田之往記，考阡陌於前書。

translations.literal: I seek the old records of the well-field, examine the front books on field paths.
translations.idiomatic: I follow the well-field in old annals and read the former texts on field and path.

sentences.zh: 顏簞食而樂在，鄭高廩而空虛。

translations.literal: Yan Hui had a bamboo basket yet joy remained; Zheng's high granaries stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui ate from a bamboo basket and was glad; Zheng filled the high granary and still stood empty.

sentences.zh: 頃四百而不足，畝五十而有餘。

translations.literal: A whole district's four hundred was not enough; fifty per mu yet had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred for the district was too little; fifty per mu still left plenty.

sentences.zh: 撫幽衷而跼念，幸取給於庭廬。

translations.literal: I stroke my hidden heart and brood cramped, fortunate to be fed from the courtyard's thatched shelters.
translations.idiomatic: I press a cramped sorrow in my breast, glad to be fed from the thatch by the yard.

sentences.zh: 緯東菑之故耜，浸北畝之新渠。

translations.literal: I warp the eastern furrow's old plough, soak the northern field's new ditch.
translations.idiomatic: I set the eastern furrow's old plough, flood the northern field's new channel.

sentences.zh: 無褰爨於曉蓐，不抱惄於朝蔬。

translations.literal: No lifting the cooking pot at dawn bedding, no cradling hunger at morning greens.
translations.idiomatic: No pot lifted at dawn on the rush mat, no hunger nursed over the morning greens.

sentences.zh: 排外物以齊遣，獨爲累之在余。

translations.literal: I cast off outer things to align my letting-go, alone the burden rests on me.
translations.idiomatic: I cast outer things aside to match my release—only on me does the burden lie.

sentences.zh: 安事千斯之積，不羨汶陽之墟。

translations.literal: Why envy a thousand stores heaped high? I do not envy the fields of Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Why envy barns stacked a thousand deep? I do not covet Wenyang's fields.

sentences.zh: 臨巽維而騁目，卽堆塚而流眄。

translations.literal: I gaze toward the southeast domain and let my eyes run free, then turn to the mound-tombs and let my glance stream on.
translations.idiomatic: I look to the southeast and let the eye run free, then to the mound-tombs and let the gaze pour on.

sentences.zh: 雖茲山之培塿，乃文靖之所宴。

translations.literal: Though this hill is but a low mound, it was where Wen Jing feasted.
translations.idiomatic: This hill is only a low mound—yet Wen Jing once feasted here.

sentences.zh: 驅四牡之低昂，響繁笳之清囀。

translations.literal: I drive the four chestnuts' rise and fall; clear panpipes answer with bright turns.
translations.idiomatic: Four chestnuts rise and fall beneath the whip; clear panpipes answer in bright turns.

sentences.zh: 羅方員而綺錯，窮海陸而兼薦。

translations.literal: Round and square vessels spread in brocade confusion; sea and land are exhausted in joint offering.
translations.idiomatic: Round and square dishes tangle like brocade; sea and land are drained in one offering.

sentences.zh: 奚一權之足偉，委千金其如線。

translations.literal: How could one shaft's splendor suffice? A thousand gold seems but a thread.
translations.idiomatic: How could one beam's grandeur suffice? A thousand in gold is thin as thread.

sentences.zh: 試撫臆而爲言，豈斯風之可扇。

translations.literal: I try to press my breast and speak: can such a wind be fanned?
translations.idiomatic: I press my breast and try to speak—can such a wind be stirred?

sentences.zh: 將通人之遠旨，非庸情之所見。

translations.literal: It will reach the far intent of the penetrating man—not a vulgar sentiment's sight.
translations.idiomatic: It reaches the far intent of the penetrating man—not what vulgar feeling sees.

sentences.zh: 聊遷情而徙睇，識方阜於歸津。

translations.literal: For a moment I shift my heart and turn my gaze, discerning the square hillock at the returning ford.
translations.idiomatic: For a moment I shift heart and turn my gaze, and know the square hill at the returning ford.

sentences.zh: 帶脩汀於桂渚，肇舉鍤於強秦。

translations.literal: A belt of level sand at Cassia Ford, first raising the spade in mighty Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Level sand belts Cassia Ford; the spade was first raised in mighty Qin.

sentences.zh: 路縈吳而款越，塗被海而通閩。

translations.literal: The road winds through Wu and knocks at Yue; the track skirts the sea and threads through Min.
translations.idiomatic: The road coils through Wu and knocks at Yue; the track skirts the sea and threads Min.

sentences.zh: 懷三鳥以長念，伊故鄉之可珍。

translations.literal: I embrace the three birds in long remembrance—how precious the old homeland is!
translations.idiomatic: I hold the three birds in long remembrance—how dear the old country is!

sentences.zh: 實褰期於晚歲，非失步於方春。

translations.literal: Truly my hope rests on the year's late span; I have not missed the step at spring's prime.
translations.idiomatic: Truly my hope waits on the year's late span; I have not missed the step in spring's prime.

sentences.zh: 何東川之濔濔，獨流涕於吾人。

translations.literal: Why does the eastern stream flow so wide—only I shed tears for our men?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the eastern stream run so wide—only I weep for our men?

sentences.zh: 謬參賢於昔代，亟徒游於茲所。

translations.literal: Wrongly I was judged worthy beside the worthies of old ages, hastening to roam at this place.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongly I was ranked among the worthies of old, hurrying to roam at this place.

sentences.zh: 侍采旄而齊轡，陪龍舟而遵渚。

translations.literal: I attended the feathered banners and matched their pace, accompanied the dragon boats along the islets.
translations.idiomatic: I waited on feathered banners and matched their pace, followed dragon boats along the islets.

sentences.zh: 或列席而賦詩，或班觴而宴語。

translations.literal: Sometimes we took ranks and composed verse; sometimes we passed cups and feasted in talk.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes we took rank and wrote verse; sometimes we passed cups and feasted in talk.

sentences.zh: 繐帷一朝冥漠，西陵忽其蔥楚。

translations.literal: The coloured curtain—one morning turned dusk-dark; the western mounds suddenly grew thick with scrub.
translations.idiomatic: The coloured curtain—one morning went dark; the western mounds suddenly choked with scrub.

sentences.zh: 望商飇而永歎，每樂愷於斯觀。

translations.literal: I gaze at the autumn gale and sigh without end, each time finding joy in this view.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze at the autumn gale and sigh without end, yet each time find joy in this view.

sentences.zh: 始則鐘石鏘珣，終以魚龍瀾漫。

translations.literal: At first bells and stones chimed bright; at last fish and dragons surged in waves.
translations.idiomatic: First bells and stones rang clear; in the end fish and dragons rolled in waves.

sentences.zh: 或升降有序，或浮白無算。

translations.literal: Some rose and fell in order; some drained their cups beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Some rose and fell in order; some drained cups beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 貴則丙、魏、蕭、曹，親則梁武、周旦。

translations.literal: Noble were Bing Ji, Wei Xiang, Xiao He, and Cao Shen; intimate were the Duke of Zhou and Liang Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Noble were Bing Ji, Wei Xiang, Xiao He, and Cao Shen; close were the Duke of Zhou and Liang Wu.

sentences.zh: 莫不共霜霧而歇滅，與風雲而消散。

translations.literal: None failed to rest with the frost-mist and perish, to scatter with wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to lie down with frost-mist and perish, to scatter with wind and cloud.

sentences.zh: 眺孫后之墓田，尋雄霸之遺武。

translations.literal: I look upon the tomb-fields of Sun's empress; I seek the martial traces of a hegemon's pride.
translations.idiomatic: I look on the tomb-fields of Sun's empress and seek a hegemon's martial traces.

sentences.zh: 實接漢之後王，信開吳之英主。

translations.literal: Truly he succeeded the kings after Han, trusted as the heroic lord who opened Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Truly he followed Han's later kings, trusted as the heroic lord who opened Wu.

sentences.zh: 指衡岳而作鎮，苞江漢而爲宇。

translations.literal: He made Heng Mountain his barrier, wrapped the Yangtze and Han as his domain.
translations.idiomatic: He set Heng Mountain as his barrier and wrapped Yangtze and Han as his realm.

sentences.zh: 徒徵言於石槨，遂延災於金縷。

translations.literal: Only to summon words from a stone coffin, and thereby prolong disaster through gold threads.
translations.idiomatic: Only to summon words from a stone coffin—and so prolong disaster through gold threads.

sentences.zh: 忽蕪穢而不脩，同原陵之膴膴。

translations.literal: Suddenly overgrown, untended—together with Yuanling's stretching mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly overgrown and untended—like Yuanling's stretching mounds.

sentences.zh: 寧知螻蟻之與狐兔，無論樵芻之與牧豎。

translations.literal: Who knew that ants and fox-rabbits matter no more than woodcutters and shepherd boys?
translations.idiomatic: Who knew ants and fox-rabbits matter no more than woodcutters and shepherd boys?

sentences.zh: 睇東巘以流目，心悽愴而不怡。

translations.literal: I gaze at the eastern hill-crest and let my eyes drift—the heart grieves and will not ease.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze at the eastern hill-crest and let the eyes drift—the heart grieves and will not ease.

sentences.zh: 蓋昔儲之舊苑，實博望之餘基。

translations.literal: This was once the old park of the heir's storehouse, truly the remnant base of Bo Wang.
translations.idiomatic: This was once the heir's old park, truly Bo Wang's remnant base.

sentences.zh: 脩林則表以桂樹，列草則冠以芳芝。

translations.literal: The trim groves were marked out with cassia trees; the ordered grasses crowned with fragrant orchids.
translations.idiomatic: Trim groves were marked with cassia; ordered grasses crowned with fragrant orchids.

sentences.zh: 風臺累翼，月榭重栭。

translations.literal: Wind terraces piled wings; moon pavilions doubled rafters.
translations.idiomatic: Wind terraces piled wing on wing; moon pavilions doubled rafters.

sentences.zh: 千櫨捷嶫，百栱相持。

translations.literal: A thousand pillars thrust swift; a hundred brackets braced each other.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand pillars shot up sharp; a hundred brackets locked together.

sentences.zh: 皁轅林駕，蘭枻水嬉。

translations.literal: Dark carriage shafts lined the forest; orchid oars played on the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Dark shafts lined the woods; orchid oars sported on the water.

sentences.zh: 逾三齡而事往，忽二紀以歷茲。

translations.literal: More than three years since affairs passed; suddenly two cycles have spanned to now.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years since affairs passed; suddenly two cycles have reached to now.

sentences.zh: 咸夷漫以蕩滌，非古今之異時。

translations.literal: All was levelled and washed by flood and sweep—not a different age from ancient to present.
translations.idiomatic: All was levelled and washed by flood and sweep—not a different age from then to now.

sentences.zh: 回余眸於艮域，覿高館於茲嶺。

translations.literal: I turn my eyes to the northeast domain, beholding the high lodge on this ridge.
translations.idiomatic: I turn my eyes to the northeast and behold the high lodge on this ridge.

sentences.zh: 雖混成以無跡，實遺訓之可秉。

translations.literal: Though merged into completion without a trace, truly the bequeathed teaching can be held.
translations.idiomatic: Though he merged into the whole and left no trace, his handed-down teaching can still be grasped.

sentences.zh: 始飡霞而吐霧，終陵虛而倒影。

translations.literal: At first he ate cloud-mist and spat fog; at last he crossed the void and cast reflections downward.
translations.idiomatic: At first he ate cloud-mist and spat fog; at last he crossed the void and cast reflections down.

sentences.zh: 駕雌蜺之連卷，泛天江之悠永。

translations.literal: He drove the rainbow-hued female serpent in rolling coils, floated on the heavenly river's long reach.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the rainbow serpent in rolling coils and floated on the heavenly river's long reach.

sentences.zh: 指咸池而一息，望瑤臺而高騁，匪爽言以自姱，冀神方之可請。

translations.literal: He pointed at Marsh Pool for one rest, gazed toward Jewelled Terrace and sped high—not flattering himself with boastful words, hoping the divine method might be sought.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at Marsh Pool for one rest, gazed at Jewelled Terrace and sped high—not boasting, hoping the divine method might be sought.

sentences.zh: 惟鐘岩之隱鬱，表皇都而作峻，蓋望秩之所宗，含風雲而吐潤。

translations.literal: Only Bell Crag's hidden mass, manifesting the imperial capital as loftiness—surely where the sacrifice-altars look, holding wind and cloud and breathing moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bell Crag's hidden mass, showing the imperial capital as loftiness—where altars look, holding wind and cloud and breathing moisture.

sentences.zh: 其爲狀也，則巍峨崇袴，喬枝拂日；

translations.literal: As to its form: towering and clasping in grandeur, tall branches brushing the sun;
translations.idiomatic: As to its form: towering, clasping in grandeur, tall branches brushing the sun;

sentences.zh: 嶢嶷岧＜上山下亭＞，墜石堆星。

translations.literal: lofty, perilous peaks and hanging crags, fallen stones piled like stars.
translations.idiomatic: lofty perilous peaks and hanging crags, fallen stones piled like stars.

sentences.zh: 岑崟峍屼，或坳或平；

translations.literal: Peak on peak, jagged and steep, now hollow now flat;
translations.idiomatic: Peak on peak, jagged and steep, now hollow, now flat;

sentences.zh: 盤堅枕臥，詭狀殊形。

translations.literal: coiled solid, pillowing recumbent, strange shapes and different forms.
translations.idiomatic: coiled hard, laid recumbent, strange shapes and alien forms.

sentences.zh: 孤嶝橫插，洞穴斜經；

translations.literal: Lone crags thrust crosswise, caves and holes slanting through;
translations.idiomatic: Lone crags jut crosswise; caves and holes cut slanting through;

sentences.zh: 千丈萬仞，三襲九成。

translations.literal: a thousand zhang, ten thousand ren, three layers and nine terraces.
translations.idiomatic: a thousand zhang high, ten thousand ren deep, three tiers and nine stages.

sentences.zh: 亘繞州邑，款跨郊坰；

translations.literal: Stretching round about the district towns, spanning across suburbs and fields;
translations.idiomatic: Stretching round district towns, spanning suburbs and fields;

sentences.zh: 素煙晚帶，白霧晨縈。

translations.literal: plain mist belts the evening, white fog curls in morning.
translations.idiomatic: plain mist belts the dusk; white fog coils at dawn.

sentences.zh: 近循則一巖異色，遠望則百嶺俱青。

translations.literal: Close along them, one crag has a different hue; gazing far, a hundred peaks are all green.
translations.idiomatic: Near at hand each crag wears its own colour; far off, a hundred peaks share one green.

sentences.zh: 觀二代之塋兆，睹摧殘之餘鹆遂。

translations.literal: I view the tombs of two dynasties, behold the remnant mesh of their destruction.
translations.idiomatic: I view two dynasties' tombs and behold the remnant mesh of their destruction.

sentences.zh: 成顛沛於虐豎，康斂衿於虛器；

translations.literal: Cheng was overturned by vicious eunuchs; Kang held his lapels before an empty throne;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng fell to vicious eunuchs; Kang smoothed his lapels before an empty throne;

sentences.zh: 穆恭已於岩廊，簡游情於玄肆；

translations.literal: Mu Gongyi was courteous already in the rocky gallery; Jian loosened his heart in the dark stalls;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Gongyi was courteous in the rocky gallery; Jian loosened his heart in the dark stalls;

sentences.zh: 烈窮飲以致災，安忘懷而受祟。

translations.literal: Lie drank to the limit and brought disaster; An forgot his cares and received bane.
translations.idiomatic: Lie drank past measure and drew disaster; An laid down care and drew harm.

sentences.zh: 何宗祖之奇傑，威橫天而陵地。

translations.literal: How extraordinary the ancestral founders—might spanning heaven, dominance over earth.
translations.idiomatic: What men were those founding ancestors—power across heaven, rule across earth.

sentences.zh: 惟聖文之纘武，殆隆平之可至。

translations.literal: Only the sage Wen continued the martial—perhaps great peace could be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Only sage Wen carried on the martial work—perhaps true peace could come.

sentences.zh: 余世德之所君，仰遺封而掩淚。

translations.literal: For generations my clan's virtue has ruled them; I look up at the ancestral tombs and veil my tears.
translations.idiomatic: For generations my clan's virtue has ruled them; I look up at ancestral tombs and veil my tears.

sentences.zh: 神寢匪一，靈館相距。

translations.literal: The spirit palaces are not one; the numinous lodges stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit halls are many, not one; numinous lodges face each other across distance.

sentences.zh: 席布騂駒，堂流桂醑。

translations.literal: Mats spread with reddish calves; halls flow with cassia wine.
translations.idiomatic: Mats spread for ruddy calves; halls stream with cassia wine.

sentences.zh: 降紫皇於天闕，延二妃於湘渚。

translations.literal: Purple Emperor descends at the heavenly gate; the two Xiang ladies are summoned at Xiang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Purple Emperor comes down at the heavenly gate; the two Xiang consorts are called at Xiang Ford.

sentences.zh: 浮蘭煙於桂棟，召巫陽於南楚。

translations.literal: Orchid smoke floats on cassia beams; Wu Yang is called to southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid smoke drifts on cassia beams; Wu Yang is summoned to southern Chu.

sentences.zh: 揚玉桴，握椒糈。

translations.literal: Jade sounding-sticks are raised; peppered millet is grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Jade clappers lift; peppered millet is taken in hand.

sentences.zh: 怳臨風以浩唱，折瓊茅而延佇。

translations.literal: As if chanting to the wind in vast song, breaking cassia grass and lingering long.
translations.idiomatic: As though singing vast songs into the wind, breaking cassia grass and standing long.

sentences.zh: 敬惟空路邈遠，神蹤遐闊。

translations.literal: Reverently—the void road is remote; divine tracks stretch far.
translations.idiomatic: In reverence—the void road is far; the divine trace stretches farther still.

sentences.zh: 念甚驚飆，生猶聚沫。

translations.literal: I think how startling is the gale; life is still foam clustered.
translations.idiomatic: I think how sharp the sudden gale is; living is still clustered foam.

sentences.zh: 歸妙軫於一乘，啓玄扉於三達。

translations.literal: Return the subtle carriage to one vehicle; open the dark door on three roads.
translations.idiomatic: Bring the subtle carriage back to one conveyance; open the dark gate on three paths.

sentences.zh: 欲息心以遣累，必違人而後豁。

translations.literal: If you wish to calm the heart and shed burdens, you must leave the crowd—only then is it open.
translations.idiomatic: To quiet the heart and cast off burdens, you must turn from the crowd—only then does it clear.

sentences.zh: 或結郐愰於岩根，或開欞於木末。

translations.literal: Some knot a thatched hut at the rock's root, some open a lattice window at the tree's crown.
translations.idiomatic: Some tie a thatched hut to the rock's foot, some open a lattice window in the tree's crown.

sentences.zh: 室闇蘿蔦，簷梢松栝。

translations.literal: The room is dim with creeping vines; the eaves trail pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: The room dims with creeping vines; pine and cypress trail from the eaves.

sentences.zh: 旣得理於兼謝，固忘懷於飢渴。

translations.literal: Having gained principle in mutual leaving behind, firmly forgetting hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Once principle came through mutual release, hunger and thirst were firmly forgotten.

sentences.zh: 或攀枝獨遠，或陵雲高蹈。

translations.literal: Some clamber branches alone into distance; some tread clouds in high steps.
translations.idiomatic: Some climb branches alone into the far; some walk clouds in high steps.

sentences.zh: 因葺茨以結名，猶觀空以表號。

translations.literal: By thatching huts they make a name; still, gazing at emptiness they take a title.
translations.idiomatic: They make a name by thatching huts; still they take a title by gazing at emptiness.

sentences.zh: 得忘己於茲日，豈期心於來報。

translations.literal: On this day one may forget oneself—who could expect the heart's return in time to come?
translations.idiomatic: Today one may forget the self—who could expect the heart's return in days to come?

sentences.zh: 天假餘以大德，荷茲賜之無疆。

translations.literal: Heaven lent me great virtue, bearing this gift without boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven lent me great virtue and loaded me with a gift without boundary.

sentences.zh: 受老夫之嘉稱，班燕禮於上庠。

translations.literal: I received the old gentleman's fine praise, and banquet rites were conferred at the upper school.
translations.idiomatic: I took the old gentleman's fine praise, and banquet rites were set at the upper school.

sentences.zh: 無希驥之秀質，乏如圭之令望。

translations.literal: I have not the fine substance of a thousand-li steed, nor the fair prospect of a jade sceptre.
translations.idiomatic: I lack the thousand-li steed's fine substance and the jade sceptre's fair prospect.

sentences.zh: 邀昔恩於舊主，重匪服於今皇。

translations.literal: I invite the former grace of the old lord, again receiving unfit robes from today's emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I call back the old lord's former grace, yet again take unfit robes from today's emperor.

sentences.zh: 仰休老之盛則，請微軀於夕陽。

translations.literal: I look up at the flourishing rule of honouring the aged, asking that this slight frame rest in the setting sun.
translations.idiomatic: I look up at the flourishing rule that honours age and ask this slight frame to rest in the setting sun.

sentences.zh: 勞蒙司而獲謝，猶奉職於春坊。

translations.literal: Though toiling at the ministry gate I gained dismissal, still I held office in the spring palace.
translations.idiomatic: Though I toiled at the ministry gate and won dismissal, I still held office in the spring palace.

sentences.zh: 時言歸於陋宇，聊暇日以翱翔。

translations.literal: Then words turned toward my humble dwelling; for a time I had leisure days to soar.
translations.idiomatic: Then speech turned toward my humble house; for a while I had leisure days to wander.

sentences.zh: 棲余志於淨國，歸余心於道場。

translations.literal: My will nests in the pure land; my heart returns to the dharma field.
translations.idiomatic: My will nests in the pure land; my heart goes home to the dharma field.

sentences.zh: 獸依墀而莫駭，魚牣沼而不綱。

translations.literal: Beasts crouch by the terrace and do not startle; fish fill the pool yet nets are not cast.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts crouch by the terrace unstartled; fish fill the pool and no net is cast.

sentences.zh: 旋迷塗於去轍，篤後念於徂光。

translations.literal: I turn back on the lost track of departing wheel-ruts, fix deep thought on the light of setting forth.
translations.idiomatic: I turn from the lost track of departing ruts and fix deep thought on the light of going forth.

sentences.zh: 晚樹開花，初英落蕊。

translations.literal: Late trees open with flowers; first blossoms drop their pistils.
translations.idiomatic: Late trees break into flower; first blossoms shed their pistils.

sentences.zh: 或異林而分丹青，乍因風而雜紅紫。

translations.literal: Sometimes different groves split green and red; suddenly wind mixes scarlet and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes separate groves split green from red; suddenly wind mingles scarlet and purple.

sentences.zh: 紫蓮夜發，紅荷曉舒。

translations.literal: Purple lotus blooms by night; red lotus opens at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Purple lotus flowers at night; red lotus opens with dawn.

sentences.zh: 輕風微動，其芳襲余。

translations.literal: A light breeze stirs slightly, its fragrance reaching me.
translations.idiomatic: A light breeze stirs; its fragrance reaches me.

sentences.zh: 風騷屑於園樹，月籠連於池竹。

translations.literal: The wind rasps through garden trees; moonlight blankets pond bamboo in one sheet.
translations.idiomatic: Wind rustles in garden trees; moonlight blankets the pond bamboo.

sentences.zh: 蔓長柯於簷桂，髮黃華於庭菊。

translations.literal: Vines extend branches over eaves and cassia; yellow blooms break forth on courtyard chrysanthemums.
translations.idiomatic: Vines stretch along eaves-cassia; yellow blooms open on courtyard chrysanthemums.

sentences.zh: 冰懸埳而帶坻，雪縈松而被野。

translations.literal: Ice hangs from banks and rims the islets; snow winds round pines and clothes the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Ice hangs from banks and rims the islets; snow winds round pines and covers the wild.

sentences.zh: 鴨屯飛而不散，雁高翔而欲下。

translations.literal: Ducks mass in flight yet do not scatter; geese soar high, about to descend.
translations.idiomatic: Ducks mass in flight without scattering; geese wheel high, about to alight.

sentences.zh: 並時物之可懷，雖外來而非假。

translations.literal: All the season's things are worth cherishing; though from outside, none are borrowed affectation.
translations.idiomatic: All the season offers is worth cherishing; though from outside, none is sham.

sentences.zh: 𢉴情性之所留滯，亦志之而不能捨也。

translations.literal: What the disposition holds and lingers over, the will too cannot cast away.
translations.idiomatic: What one's nature holds and lingers over, the will too cannot cast away.

sentences.zh: 傷余情之頹暮，罹憂患其相溢。

translations.literal: My feelings grieve at age's decline; calamity and sorrow together overflow.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that feeling fades with age; trouble and sorrow overflow together.

sentences.zh: 悲異軫而同歸，歎殊方而並失。

translations.literal: Sadly different chariots reach the same end; sighing that separate paths are lost alike.
translations.idiomatic: Sadly different roads reach one end; sighing that far-apart paths are lost alike.

sentences.zh: 時復託情魚鳥，歸閑蓬蓽。

translations.literal: At times I entrust feeling to fish and birds, returning to leisure in a thatched hut.
translations.idiomatic: At times I give my heart to fish and birds, returning to leisure in a thatched hut.

sentences.zh: 旁闕吳娃，前無趙瑟。

translations.literal: Beside me no Wu beauty; before me no Zhao zither.
translations.idiomatic: No Wu beauty at my side; no Zhao zither before me.

sentences.zh: 以斯終老，於焉消日。

translations.literal: With this I shall end my days, here passing the hours.
translations.idiomatic: With this I shall end my days, here passing my hours.

sentences.zh: 惟以天地之恩不報，書事之官靡述；

translations.literal: Only that Heaven and Earth's favor goes unrequited, and no recorder of affairs sets it down;
translations.idiomatic: Only Heaven and Earth's favor goes unrequited, and no court historian records it;

sentences.zh: 徒重於高門之地，不載於良史之筆。

translations.literal: I merely weigh in a great house, yet win no line from fine historians' brushes.
translations.idiomatic: I merely rank among great houses, yet earn no line in fine histories.

sentences.zh: 長太息其何言，羌愧心之非一。

translations.literal: Long I sigh—what more is there to say? Alas, my heart's shame is not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: Long I sigh—what more is there to say? Alas, shame in the heart is not one alone.

sentences.zh: 尋加特進，光祿、侍中、少傅如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Special Advance, retaining Grand Master for Splendor, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received Special Advance, keeping Grand Master for Splendor, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒官，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office at seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he died in office at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官，賻錢五萬，布百匹，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: An edict granted his former offices, funeral cash of fifty thousand, a hundred bolts of cloth, posthumous title Yin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his former offices, fifty thousand cash in funeral gifts, a hundred bolts of cloth, posthumous title Yin.

sentences.zh: 約左目重瞳子，腰有紫志，聰明過人。

translations.literal: Yue's left eye had double pupils; a purple mark on his waist—intelligence surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's left eye had double pupils and a purple mark on his waist; his intelligence surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 好墳籍，聚書至二萬卷，京師莫比。

translations.literal: He loved tombs and archives, gathered books to twenty thousand scrolls—none in the capital compared.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics, gathered books to twenty thousand scrolls—none in the capital compared.

sentences.zh: 少時孤貧，丐于宗黨，得米數百斛，爲宗人所侮，覆米而去。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he begged among kin, got several hundred hu of rice, was insulted by clansmen, and overturned the rice and left.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he begged among kin for several hundred hu of rice; clansmen insulted him, so he overturned the rice and left.

sentences.zh: 及貴，不以爲憾，用爲郡部傳。

translations.literal: When exalted he held no grudge, and the story was used in district gazetteers.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose high he held no grudge; the tale was used in the district gazetteers.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍讌，有妓師是齊文惠宮人。

translations.literal: Once attending a feast, a musician was a palace woman of Qi Emperor Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast, a musician had been a palace woman of Qi Emperor Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 帝問識座中客不？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked whether she knew any guest at the table.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked whether she knew any guest present.

sentences.zh: 曰：「惟識沈家令。

translations.literal: She said, "I know only Master Shen of the Shen household.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I know only Master Shen.

sentences.zh: 」約伏座流涕，帝亦悲焉，爲之罷酒。

translations.literal: " Yue bowed at his seat and wept; the Emperor too was saddened and ended the wine.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue bowed at his seat and wept; the Emperor too was moved and stopped the feast.

sentences.zh: 約歷仕三代，該悉舊章，博物洽聞，當世取則。

translations.literal: Yue served three dynasties, mastered old statutes, was broadly learned and well informed—the age took him as its model.
translations.idiomatic: Yue served three dynasties, mastered old statutes, and was broadly learned—the age took him as its standard.

sentences.zh: 謝玄暉善爲詩，任彥昇工於文章，約兼而有之，然不能過也。

translations.literal: Xie Xuanyuan excelled at poetry, Ren Yansheng at literary composition—Yue had both yet could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuanyuan excelled in poetry and Ren Yansheng in prose—Yue had both yet could not surpass either.

sentences.zh: 自負高才，昧於榮利，乘時藉勢，頗累清談。

translations.literal: Proud of great talent, blind to glory and profit, he rode the times and borrowed power—quite to the cost of pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of towering talent, blind to rank and gain, he rode the times and borrowed power—much to the harm of pure discourse.

sentences.zh: 及居端揆，稍弘止足。

translations.literal: Once he stood at the top, he somewhat broadened restraint and sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the summit of office, he showed some regard for restraint.

sentences.zh: 每進一官，輒殷勤請退，而終不能去，論者方之山濤。

translations.literal: Each promotion he earnestly asked to retire, yet in the end could not leave—commentators compared him to Shan Tao.
translations.idiomatic: At each promotion he earnestly asked to retire yet could never leave—men compared him to Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 用事十餘年，未嘗有所薦達，政之得失，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: In power more than ten years, he never advanced anyone; on policy's gains or losses he only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: In power more than ten years he never advanced anyone; on policy he only murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖有憾於張稷，及稷卒，因與約言之。

translations.literal: At first Gaozu bore resentment against Zhang Ji; when Ji died he spoke of it with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gaozu resented Zhang Ji; when Ji died he spoke of it with Yue.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「尚書左僕射出作邊州刺史，已往之事，何足復論。

translations.literal: Yue said, "The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing going out as a border inspector—past matters, what need to discuss again?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "A left vice director sent out as a border inspector—past matters, what need discuss them again?

sentences.zh: 」帝以爲婚家相爲，大怒曰：「卿言如此，是忠臣邪！

translations.literal: " The Emperor, thinking families by marriage shielding one another, raged: "You speak thus—are you a loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, thinking it kin shielding kin, raged: "You speak thus—are you a loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 」乃輦歸內殿。

translations.literal: " He was borne back to the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He was borne back to the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 約懼，不覺高祖起，猶坐如初。

translations.literal: Yue was afraid, did not notice Gaozu rise, and still sat as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was afraid; not noticing Gaozu had risen, he still sat as before.

sentences.zh: 及還，未至床，而憑空頓於戶下。

translations.literal: When he returned, before reaching the couch he pitched forward empty in the air and fell by the door.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, before he reached the couch he pitched forward and fell by the door.

sentences.zh: 因病，夢齊和帝以劍斷其舌。

translations.literal: In illness he dreamed Emperor He of Qi cut his tongue with a sword.
translations.idiomatic: Sick, he dreamed Qi Emperor He cut his tongue with a sword.

sentences.zh: 召巫視之，巫言如夢。

translations.literal: He summoned a shaman to look; the shaman spoke as the dream.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a shaman; the shaman spoke as in the dream.

sentences.zh: 乃呼道士奏赤章於天，稱禪代之事，不由己出。

translations.literal: He then called Daoists to present red writs to Heaven, saying the abdication affair had not issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: He called Daoists to present red writs to Heaven, claiming the dynastic change had not come from him.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣上省醫徐奘視約疾，還具以狀聞。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Palace Physician Xu Zang to view Yue's illness; returning he reported it in full.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent palace physician Xu Zang to examine Yue; returning, he reported everything.

sentences.zh: 先此，約嘗侍讌，值豫州獻栗，徑寸半，帝奇之，問曰：「栗事多少？

translations.literal: Before this, Yue once attended a feast when Yuzhou presented chestnuts an inch and a half across; the Emperor marveled and asked, "How much is there to the matter of chestnuts?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yue had attended a feast when Yuzhou presented chestnuts an inch and a half across; the Emperor marveled and asked, "How much is there to say of chestnuts?

sentences.zh: 」與約各疏所憶，少帝三事。

translations.literal: " He and Yue each wrote what they recalled—the Emperor had three things fewer.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Yue each wrote what they recalled—the Emperor fell three items short.

sentences.zh: 出謂人曰：「此公護前，不讓卽羞死。

translations.literal: Going out he told someone, "This gentleman guards his pride—if he does not yield he would die of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, he told someone, "This man guards his pride—he would die of shame rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 」帝以其言不遜，欲抵其罪，徐勉固諫乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, taking his words as insubordinate, wished to punish him; Xu Mian firmly remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, finding the words insubordinate, meant to punish him; Xu Mian firmly remonstrated and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 及聞赤章事，大怒，中使譴責者數焉，約懼遂卒。

translations.literal: When he heard of the red writ matter he was greatly angry; palace envoys rebuked him several times—Yue in fear then died.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the red writ, he was furious; palace envoys rebuked him repeatedly—Yue died in fear.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰文，帝曰：「懷情不盡曰隱。

translations.literal: The offices gave posthumous title Wen; the Emperor said, "Holding feeling back without exhausting it is called Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The offices proposed posthumous title Wen; the Emperor said, "Holding feeling without exhausting it is called Yin.

sentences.zh: 」故改爲隱云。

translations.literal: " So it was changed to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " So it was changed to Yin.

sentences.zh: 所著《晉書》百一十卷，《宋書》百卷，《齊紀》二十卷，《高祖紀》十四卷，《邇言》十卷，《諡例》十卷，《宋文章志》三十卷，文集一百卷：皆行於世。

translations.literal: His writings: History of Jin in one hundred and ten scrolls, History of Song in one hundred scrolls, Annals of Qi in twenty scrolls, Annals of the High Ancestor in fourteen scrolls, Near Words in ten scrolls, Posthumous Examples in ten scrolls, Literary Records of Song in thirty scrolls, and collected works in one hundred scrolls—all circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote History of Jin in 110 scrolls, History of Song in 100, Annals of Qi in 20, Annals of the High Ancestor in 14, Near Words in 10, Posthumous Examples in 10, Literary Records of Song in 30, and collected works in 100—all circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 又撰《四聲譜》，以爲在昔詞人，累千載而不寤，而獨得胸衿，窮其妙旨，自謂入神之作，高祖雅不好焉。

translations.literal: He also compiled Rhymes in Four Tones, thinking poets of old for a thousand years had not understood, while he alone grasped the subtle intent in his breast—a work he called divine—Gaozu greatly disliked it.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Rhymes in Four Tones, holding that poets for a millennium had not understood tones while he alone had grasped their subtlety—a work he called divine—Gaozu disliked it greatly.

sentences.zh: 帝問周捨曰：「何謂四聲？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Zhou She: "What are the four tones?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Zhou She, "What are the four tones?

sentences.zh: 」舍曰：「天子聖哲」是也，然帝竟不遵用。

translations.literal: " She said: "The Son of Heaven is sage and wise"—that is it; yet the Emperor in the end did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "The Son of Heaven is sage and wise"—that is it; yet the Emperor never adopted it.

sentences.zh: 子旋，及約時已歷中書侍郎，永嘉太守，司徒從事中郎，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His son Xuan; while Yue lived he had already served as Secretariat Gentleman, Administrator of Yongjia, Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Prince's staff, and Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan; while Yue lived he had already been Secretariat Gentleman, Yongjia administrator, staff attendant of the Masters of Writing, and right chief clerk of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 免約喪，爲太子僕，復以母憂去官，而蔬食辟穀。

translations.literal: When Yue's mourning ended he was made Crown Prince's Household Steward; again he left office for his mother's mourning and ate vegetables while fasting.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue's mourning ended he was made crown prince steward; again he left office for his mother's mourning and lived on vegetables while fasting.

sentences.zh: 服除，猶絕粳粱。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he still abstained from polished grain.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he still abstained from polished grain.

sentences.zh: 爲給事黃門侍郎、中撫軍長史。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate and Chief Clerk of the Central Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate and chief clerk of the Central Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 出爲招遠將軍、南康內史，在部以清治稱。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Draws the Distant and Administrator of Nankang; in the commandery he was known for pure governance.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Draws the Distant and administrator of Nankang; in office he was known for pure governance.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰恭侯。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title Respectful Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous title Respectful Marquis.

sentences.zh: 子𢉴嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：昔木德將謝，昏嗣流虐，惵惵黔黎，命懸晷漏。

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In old times the virtue of wood was about to fade; a dim successor spread cruelty, and the trembling black-haired people hung their lives on the sundial's drip.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: When the virtue of wood was fading, a dim heir spread cruelty, and the trembling people hung their lives on the sundial's drip.

sentences.zh: 高祖義拯橫潰，志寧區夏，謀謨帷幄，實寄良、平。

translations.literal: Gaozu by righteousness rescued the collapsing flood, his will to settle the central lands; stratagems in the tent truly rested on men like Zhang Liang and Chen Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu by righteousness rescued the flood of collapse and willed to settle the realm; stratagems in the tent truly rested on men like Zhang Liang and Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 至於范雲、沈約，參預締構，贊成帝業；

translations.literal: As for Fan Yun and Shen Yue, they took part in founding and helped complete the imperial enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: As for Fan Yun and Shen Yue, they joined in founding and helped complete the imperial enterprise;

sentences.zh: 加雲以機警明贍，濟務益時，約高才博洽，名亞遷、董，俱屬興運，蓋一代之英偉焉。

translations.literal: add Yun's keen alertness and clear sufficiency in aiding affairs and benefiting the age, and Yue's towering talent and broad learning, his name second only to Sima Qian and Dong Zhongshu—both belonged to a rising fortune; they were the heroic giants of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was keen and clear in aiding affairs; Yue had towering talent and broad learning, his name second only to Qian and Dong—both rode a rising fortune; they were a generation's giants.
